170def _safe_filename(text: str) -> str: 

171 return "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in str(text))

174def _step_screen(options: tuple[str, ...], delta: int) -> None: 

175 """Move the multipart navigator without touching the parent trial picker.""" 

176 if not options: 

177 return 

178 current = str(st.session_state.get("single_screen_id", options[0])) 

179 position = options.index(current) if current in options else 0 

180 st.session_state["single_screen_id"] = options[ 

181 max(0, min(len(options) - 1, position + delta)) 

182 ] 

183

185def _render_screen_navigator(catalog: pd.DataFrame) -> Optional[str]: 

186 """Compact previous/select/next navigator for one logical multipart trial.""" 

187 if catalog.empty: 

188 st.session_state.pop("single_screen_id", None) 

189 return None 

190 options = tuple(catalog[SCREEN_ID].astype(str)) 

191 current = st.session_state.get("single_screen_id") 

192 if current not in options: 

193 st.session_state["single_screen_id"] = options[0] 

194 labels = { 

195 str( 

196 row.screen_id 

197 ): f"{int(row.screen_index)} of {len(catalog)} · {row.screen_id}" 

198 for row in catalog.itertuples() 

199 } 

200 previous, picker, following = st.columns([0.7, 5, 0.7], vertical_alignment="bottom") 

201 position = options.index(str(st.session_state["single_screen_id"])) 

202 previous.button( 

203 "◀", 

204 key="single_screen_previous", 

205 help="Previous screen in this logical trial", 

206 disabled=position == 0, 

207 on_click=_step_screen, 

208 args=(options, -1), 

209 width="stretch", 

210 ) 

211 selected = picker.selectbox( 

212 "Screen", 

213 options, 

214 key="single_screen_id", 

215 format_func=labels.get, 

216 help="One coordinate space at a time; the parent trial selection stays fixed.", 

217 ) 

218 following.button( 

219 "▶", 

220 key="single_screen_next", 

221 help="Next screen in this logical trial", 

222 disabled=position == len(options) - 1, 

223 on_click=_step_screen, 

224 args=(options, 1), 

225 width="stretch", 

226 ) 

227 return str(selected)

235def _render_true_scale_chart( 

236 fig, *, key: str, max_height: Optional[int] = None 

237) -> None: 

238 """Display a spatial figure true-to-scale, fitted to the column width. 

239 

240 ``st.plotly_chart`` pins the chart width to the column but keeps the layout 

241 height, re-laying-out the plot to an unknown scale — which breaks the 

242 data→pixel sizing the word labels were computed for (text over/under fills 

243 the boxes). Instead we render the figure at its exact pixel size, then scale 

244 that whole block *uniformly* with a CSS transform so it fills the column 

245 width. A uniform transform keeps boxes, fixations and text locked at one true 

246 scale (unlike a Plotly re-layout, which leaves the font fixed), so the plot 

247 stays faithful to the experiment at any column width — and never needs 

248 horizontal scrolling. It is only scaled down to fit (capped at 1×), so on a 

249 wide monitor it sits at true size with margin rather than being stretched. 

250 

251 ``max_height`` caps the rendered (scaled) height in px — used for the small 

252 multiples in the *Multiple Comparison* grid, where the figure should also 

253 shrink to fit a fixed cell height (whichever of width/height binds), and the 

254 iframe is sized to that cap so panels don't leave a tall band of whitespace. 

255 """ 

256 width = int(fig.layout.width or 900) 

257 height = int(fig.layout.height or 600) 

258 # VIZ-10: an animation built with autoplay on carries its per-frame duration on 

259 # the figure; kick off `Plotly.animate` at that speed after mount (Plotly's own 

260 # `auto_play` would ignore the configured speed). `None` for static figures or 

261 # autoplay-off animations → the built-in `auto_play=False` keeps them paused. 

262 autoplay_ms = animation_autoplay_frame_duration(fig) 

263 autoplay_script = ( 

264 animation_autoplay_post_script(autoplay_ms) if autoplay_ms is not None else None 

265 ) 

266 plot_html = fig.to_html( 

267 include_plotlyjs="cdn", 

268 full_html=False, 

269 config={"responsive": False, "displaylogo": False}, 

270 div_id=f"truescale-{key}", 

271 # to_html defaults to auto_play=True, which auto-runs an animated figure on 

272 # load at Plotly's default frame duration (ignoring the configured playback 

273 # speed). Start paused so the animation only plays — at the right speed — 

274 # either via the autoplay kickoff below or when the user presses Play. No 

275 # effect on static (frame-less) figures. 

276 auto_play=False, 

277 post_script=autoplay_script, 

278 ) 

279 # Scale factor: shrink to the available width, and (when capped) also to the 

280 # cell height, never upscaling past 1×. 

281 if max_height is not None: 

282 scale_js = f"Math.min(1, avail / W, {int(max_height)} / H)" 

283 iframe_height = int(max_height) + 12 

284 else: 

285 scale_js = "Math.min(1, avail / W)" 

286 iframe_height = height + 12 

287 # Wrap the fixed-size plot and scale it to the available (iframe) width. 

288 # transform-origin top-left keeps it flush-left; the outer box height tracks 

289 # the scaled height so there's no dead space below. 

290 html = f""" 

291 <div id="fit-{key}" style="width:100%;overflow:hidden;"> 

292 <div id="box-{key}" style="width:{width}px;height:{height}px; 

293 transform-origin:top left;">{plot_html}</div> 

294 </div> 

295 <script> 

296 (function() {{ 

297 var W = {width}, H = {height}; 

298 var outer = document.getElementById("fit-{key}"); 

299 var box = document.getElementById("box-{key}"); 

300 function fit() {{ 

301 var avail = outer.clientWidth || W; 

302 var s = {scale_js}; 

303 box.style.transform = "scale(" + s + ")"; 

304 outer.style.height = Math.round(H * s) + "px"; 

305 }} 

306 fit(); 

307 window.addEventListener("resize", fit); 

308 setTimeout(fit, 150); 

309 }})(); 

310 </script> 

311 """ 

312 # Iframe height = full true height (or the cap); the script trims the 

313 # visible block to the scaled height. 

314 _embed_html_iframe(html, height=iframe_height)

317def _trial_text_id(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> Optional[str]: 

318 """Best-available text identifier for a trial's words (for same-text checks).""" 

319 for col in ("unique_text_id", "text_id"): 

320 if col in trial_words.columns and not trial_words.empty: 

321 value = trial_words[col].iloc[0] 

322 if pd.notna(value): 

323 return str(value) 

324 return None

327_MIME_FOR_FORMAT = { 

328 "PNG": "image/png", 

329 "SVG": "image/svg+xml", 

330 "PDF": "application/pdf", 

331 "HTML": "text/html", 

332}

335def _render_save_plot_button( 

336 fig, 

337 *, 

338 canvas_width: int, 

339 canvas_height: int, 

340 slug: str, 

341 key_prefix: str, 

342) -> None: 

343 """Download the currently displayed figure. 

344 

345 HTML is cheap (no Kaleido/Chrome) so it downloads in a single click. PNG/SVG/ 

346 PDF go through Kaleido, which spins up a headless Chrome — far too slow to run 

347 on every Streamlit rerun — so those keep a Render step and reveal the download 

348 only once the image is ready. Width/height come from the figure's own layout 

349 so stacked / multi-panel figures save at their on-screen size. 

350 """ 

351 if fig is None: 

352 return 

353 file_stem = f"scanpath_{_safe_filename(slug)}" 

354 # Stacked (not columned) so the controls fit the narrow side-panel "Export" 

355 # toggle they now live in. 

356 fmt = st.radio( 

357 "Download format", 

358 # HTML is a browser-free fallback (no Kaleido/Chrome) — useful on 

359 # Streamlit Cloud where static image export needs a Chromium binary. 

360 options=["PNG", "SVG", "PDF", "HTML"], 

361 index=0, 

362 horizontal=True, 

363 key=f"{key_prefix}_save_format", 

364 help="PNG/SVG/PDF need a Chrome/Chromium browser (Kaleido). HTML " 

365 "is interactive and needs no browser.", 

366 ) 

367 

368 # HTML: one-click download — no expensive render to defer. 

369 if fmt == "HTML": 

370 html_bytes = fig.to_html(include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=True).encode("utf-8") 

371 st.download_button( 

372 "⬇ Download HTML", 

373 data=html_bytes, 

374 file_name=f"{file_stem}.html", 

375 mime=_MIME_FOR_FORMAT["HTML"], 

376 key=f"{key_prefix}_save_button_html", 

377 ) 

378 return 

379 

380 # PNG/SVG/PDF: render on click (Kaleido/Chrome), then reveal the download. 

381 # The signature includes the complete figure JSON and every exporter option, 

382 # so the durable result survives harmless reruns but can never leak across a 

383 # trial, format, scale, size, or visual-setting change (EXP-6). 

384 fig_width = int(fig.layout.width or canvas_width) 

385 fig_height = int(fig.layout.height or canvas_height) 

386 scale = 3 if fmt == "PNG" else 1 

387 sig = static_export_signature( 

388 fig, 

389 fmt=fmt, 

390 width=fig_width, 

391 height=fig_height, 

392 scale=scale, 

393 ) 

394 cache_key = f"_{key_prefix}_static_export_cache" 

395 inflight_key = f"_{key_prefix}_static_export_inflight" 

396 cache = st.session_state.get(cache_key) 

397 if cache and cache.get("sig") != sig: 

398 st.session_state.pop(cache_key, None) 

399 cache = None 

400 

401 generate = st.button( 

402 f"Render {fmt}", 

403 key=f"{key_prefix}_save_generate", 

404 help="Renders the image (needs Chrome/Kaleido); the download button " 

405 "appears once it's ready.", 

406 disabled=st.session_state.get(inflight_key) == sig, 

407 ) 

408 if generate: 

409 status_box = st.status("Preparing export…", expanded=True) 

410 

411 def _on_status(status: ExportStatus) -> None: 

412 elapsed = f" · {status.elapsed_s:.1f}s" if status.elapsed_s else "" 

413 state = ( 

414 "complete" 

415 if status.stage == ExportStage.READY 

416 else "error" 

417 if status.stage == ExportStage.ERROR 

418 else "running" 

419 ) 

420 status_box.update(label=f"{status.message}{elapsed}", state=state) 

421 

422 st.session_state[inflight_key] = sig 

423 try: 

424 data = render_static_figure_bytes( 

425 fig, 

426 fmt=fmt.lower(), 

427 width=fig_width, 

428 height=fig_height, 

429 scale=scale, 

430 status_callback=_on_status, 

431 ) 

432 except Exception as exc: 

433 st.session_state.pop(cache_key, None) 

434 hint = ( 

435 CHROME_INSTALL_HINT 

436 if not chrome_available() 

437 else "On Streamlit Cloud Chrome is installed via `packages.txt`; if it " 

438 "still fails, choose the **HTML** format above — it needs no browser." 

439 ) 

440 detail = str(exc) 

441 message = f"Could not render {fmt}: {detail}" 

442 # The renderer's missing-browser exception already contains the 

443 # actionable hint. Appending it again produced two identical yellow 

444 # paragraphs in the export panel (EXP-6 review feedback). 

445 if hint not in detail: 

446 message += f"\n\n{hint}" 

447 st.warning(message) 

448 cache = None 

449 else: 

450 cache = {"sig": sig, "data": data, "fmt": fmt} 

451 st.session_state[cache_key] = cache 

452 finally: 

453 st.session_state.pop(inflight_key, None) 

454 

455 if cache and cache.get("sig") == sig: 

456 data = cache["data"] 

457 st.success(f"{fmt} ready · {len(data) / 1024:.0f} KB") 

458 st.download_button( 

459 f"⬇ Download {fmt}", 

460 data=data, 

461 file_name=f"{file_stem}.{fmt.lower()}", 

462 mime=_MIME_FOR_FORMAT[fmt], 

463 key=f"{key_prefix}_save_button", 

464 ) 

465 

466 

467# Above this many frames, offer to cap the rendered frame count: each frame is a 

468# headless-Chrome render (~0.1-0.25 s), so a long reading would otherwise spin for 

469# a minute or more. Capping holds each kept frame proportionally longer, so the 

470# clip's total duration is unchanged. 

471_ANIM_FRAME_CAP = 250 

472# Rough per-frame render cost (warm browser) + one-off browser cold start, for the 

473# "~Ns to render" estimate. Approximate by design. 

474_ANIM_RENDER_S_PER_FRAME = 0.18 

475_ANIM_RENDER_COLD_START_S = 3.0 

476

478def _render_animation_export(fig, *, file_stem: str, playback_ms: float) -> None: 

479 """Export the animated scanpath as interactive HTML or a rasterized GIF/MP4. 

480 

481 HTML is one click (no browser needed to generate, keeps interactivity). GIF and 

482 MP4 rasterize every frame through Kaleido (headless Chrome) — too slow to run on 

483 every rerun — so they follow the same Render-then-download pattern as the static 

484 image export, with a progress bar and a result cached in session state so the 

485 download button survives reruns (and a re-render isn't needed unless an option 

486 changes). The clip reproduces the on-screen Play: every frame held for the same 

487 average duration, so its runtime equals the quoted playback time. 

488 """ 

489 n_frames = len(fig.frames or ()) 

490 fmt = st.radio( 

491 "Export format", 

492 options=["HTML", "GIF", "MP4"], 

493 index=0, 

494 horizontal=True, 

495 key="anim_export_format", 

496 help=( 

497 "HTML keeps the interactive play/slider and needs no browser to " 

498 "generate. GIF and MP4 are self-playing clips (great for slides or " 

499 "papers) rendered via Kaleido/Chrome — MP4 is far smaller than GIF." 

500 ), 

501 ) 

502 

503 if fmt == "HTML": 

504 # VIZ-10: the downloaded HTML must autoplay at the configured speed too 

505 # (Plotly's default auto_play ignores frame_duration), matching the live 

506 # embed + api.save_figure. Autoplay-off / static figures stay paused. 

507 autoplay_ms = animation_autoplay_frame_duration(fig) 

508 if autoplay_ms is not None: 

509 html = fig.to_html( 

510 include_plotlyjs="cdn", 

511 full_html=True, 

512 auto_play=False, 

513 post_script=animation_autoplay_post_script(autoplay_ms), 

514 ) 

515 elif fig.frames: 

516 html = fig.to_html(include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=True, auto_play=False) 

517 else: 

518 html = fig.to_html(include_plotlyjs="cdn", full_html=True) 

519 html_bytes = html.encode("utf-8") 

520 st.download_button( 

521 "⬇ Download HTML", 

522 data=html_bytes, 

523 file_name=f"{file_stem}.html", 

524 mime="text/html", 

525 key="anim_export_html", 

526 help="Self-contained HTML you can open in any browser; keeps play/slider interactivity.", 

527 ) 

528 return 

529 

530 if n_frames == 0: 

531 st.info("Nothing to animate for this trial.") 

532 return 

533 

534 # Pre-flight (ENG-10): GIF/MP4 need Chrome — warn before the user waits on a 

535 # render that can only fail, and point at the fix + the browser-free HTML. 

536 if not chrome_available(): 

537 st.warning(f"{fmt} export can't run here. {CHROME_INSTALL_HINT}", icon="⚠️") 

538 

539 frame_ms = playback_ms / n_frames if n_frames else 16.0 

540 clip_s = playback_ms / 1000.0 

541 

542 scale = st.select_slider( 

543 "Resolution", 

544 options=[0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0], 

545 value=1.0, 

546 format_func=lambda s: f"{s:g}×", 

547 key="anim_export_scale", 

548 help="Render scale: 1× matches the on-screen size. Lower is smaller/faster; " 

549 "higher is crisper/larger.", 

550 ) 

551 

552 max_frames = None 

553 if n_frames > _ANIM_FRAME_CAP: 

554 if st.checkbox( 

555 f"Limit to {_ANIM_FRAME_CAP} frames for a faster render", 

556 value=True, 

557 key="anim_export_limit", 

558 help="This reading has many fixations. Capping the rendered frames keeps " 

559 "the export quick; the clip's total duration is unchanged (each kept " 

560 "frame is held a little longer).", 

561 ): 

562 max_frames = _ANIM_FRAME_CAP 

563 

564 render_frames = min(n_frames, max_frames) if max_frames else n_frames 

565 est_s = render_frames * _ANIM_RENDER_S_PER_FRAME + _ANIM_RENDER_COLD_START_S 

566 note = f"{n_frames} frames · clip ≈ {clip_s:.1f}s · ~{est_s:.0f}s to render" 

567 if render_frames != n_frames: 

568 note += f" ({render_frames} frames rendered)" 

569 st.caption(note) 

570 if fmt == "GIF": 

571 st.caption( 

572 "GIF embeds anywhere but is large for long readings — prefer MP4, or " 

573 "lower the resolution, to shrink the file." 

574 ) 

575 

576 # Re-render only when an output-affecting input changes; otherwise reuse the 

577 # cached bytes so the download button persists across reruns. The figure's 

578 # own JSON fingerprints every visual choice that feeds the clip — trial, 

579 # playback speed, saccades/order/marker-size/background, true-to-scale text — 

580 # so toggling any of them invalidates a stale render instead of serving the 

581 # previous bytes. `scale`/`max_frames` are export-only (not in the figure), 

582 # so they're keyed separately. 

583 sig = static_export_signature( 

584 fig, 

585 fmt=fmt, 

586 width=int(fig.layout.width or 900), 

587 height=int(fig.layout.height or 600), 

588 scale=float(scale), 

589 exporter_version=( 

590 f"{EXPORTER_VERSION}:animation:{file_stem}:{max_frames}:{frame_ms:.12g}" 

591 ), 

592 ) 

593 cache = st.session_state.get("_anim_export_cache") 

594 if cache and cache.get("sig") != sig: 

595 st.session_state.pop("_anim_export_cache", None) 

596 cache = None 

597 

598 if st.button( 

599 f"Render {fmt}", 

600 key="anim_export_generate", 

601 help="Renders each frame via Kaleido (headless Chrome); the download " 

602 "appears once it's ready.", 

603 ): 

604 status_box = st.status("Preparing animation export…", expanded=True) 

605 progress_slot = st.empty() 

606 bar = None 

607 

608 def _on_status(status: ExportStatus) -> None: 

609 nonlocal bar 

610 elapsed = f" · {status.elapsed_s:.1f}s" if status.elapsed_s else "" 

611 state = ( 

612 "complete" 

613 if status.stage == ExportStage.READY 

614 else "error" 

615 if status.stage == ExportStage.ERROR 

616 else "running" 

617 ) 

618 status_box.update(label=f"{status.message}{elapsed}", state=state) 

619 if status.fraction is not None: 

620 text = ( 

621 f"{status.completed}/{status.total} frames" 

622 if status.stage == ExportStage.RASTERIZING 

623 else status.message 

624 ) 

625 if bar is None: 

626 bar = progress_slot.progress(status.fraction, text=text) 

627 else: 

628 bar.progress(status.fraction, text=text) 

629 

630 try: 

631 data = export_animation( 

632 fig, 

633 fmt=fmt.lower(), 

634 frame_duration_ms=frame_ms, 

635 scale=float(scale), 

636 max_frames=max_frames, 

637 status_callback=_on_status, 

638 ) 

639 except AnimationExportError as exc: 

640 progress_slot.empty() 

641 st.warning( 

642 f"Could not render {fmt}: {exc}\n\n" 

643 "GIF/MP4 export rasterizes each frame with a Chrome/Chromium browser " 

644 "(Kaleido). On Streamlit Cloud this is installed via `packages.txt`; " 

645 "if it still fails, use the **HTML** format above — it needs no browser." 

646 ) 

647 cache = None 

648 st.session_state.pop("_anim_export_cache", None) 

649 else: 

650 progress_slot.empty() 

651 cache = {"sig": sig, "data": data} 

652 st.session_state["_anim_export_cache"] = cache 

653 

654 if cache and cache.get("sig") == sig: 

655 data = cache["data"] 

656 size = len(data) 

657 size_label = ( 

658 f"{size / 1_048_576:.1f} MB" 

659 if size >= 1_048_576 

660 else f"{size / 1024:.0f} KB" 

661 ) 

662 st.success(f"{fmt} ready · {size_label}") 

663 st.download_button( 

664 f"⬇ Download {fmt} ({size_label})", 

665 data=data, 

666 file_name=f"{file_stem}.{fmt.lower()}", 

667 mime=mime_for(fmt.lower()), 

668 key="anim_export_download", 

669 )

672def _slice_fix_range(fix: pd.DataFrame, fix_range) -> pd.DataFrame: 

673 """Keep only fixations whose 1-based ``order_in_trial`` is within ``fix_range``. 

674 

675 ``fix_range`` is the single-trial fixation-index window (VIZ-7) — a 

676 ``(start, end)`` tuple, or ``None`` for the full trial. Applied only to the 

677 frame feeding the figure / animation / comparison builders (and thus the 

678 "This trial" export, which round-trips the on-screen figure), so the chips, 

679 panels and bulk multi-trial export keep the complete trial. A ``None`` window 

680 or a frame without ``order_in_trial`` is returned unchanged (the default path 

681 stays byte-identical).""" 

682 if ( 

683 isinstance(fix_range, (tuple, list)) 

684 and len(fix_range) == 2 

685 and fix is not None 

686 and not fix.empty 

687 and "order_in_trial" in fix.columns 

688 ): 

689 lo, hi = fix_range 

690 return fix[(fix["order_in_trial"] >= lo) & (fix["order_in_trial"] <= hi)] 

691 return fix 

692 

693 

694def _drift_corrected( 

695 fix: pd.DataFrame, words: pd.DataFrame, algorithm: Optional[str] 

696) -> pd.DataFrame: 

697 """PRE-3 vertical drift correction for one scanpath, or a true no-op. 

698 

699 Returns the very same frame **object** whenever no algorithm is selected 

700 (``None`` / ``"Off"`` — the default), or when there is nothing to correct 

701 (empty fixations or empty words). That identity matters: the caller uses 

702 ``result is fix`` to tell "corrected" from "untouched", and it guarantees the 

703 default path costs nothing and leaves every figure / cache key byte-identical. 

704 

705 Otherwise :func:`alignment.correct` snaps each fixation's ``y`` to its 

706 assigned text line and a *copy* comes back — ``fix`` is never mutated, so the 

707 raw frame stays available for the connector layer and the panels.""" 

708 if ( 

709 not algorithm 

710 or str(algorithm) == "Off" 

711 or fix is None 

712 or fix.empty 

713 or words is None 

714 or words.empty 

715 ): 

716 return fix 

717 corrected, _ = alignment.correct(fix, words, method=str(algorithm).lower()) 

718 return corrected

721def _marked_text_column(viz_settings: dict) -> Optional[str]: 

722 """The critical-span column for builders whose only marking channel is *text*. 

723 

724 ``make_scanpath_figure`` takes both ``highlight_column`` and 

725 ``critical_span_style`` and decides internally: "Mark text" recolours the word 

726 labels, "Mark border" instead draws a box overlay. The animation and 

727 comparison builders have no overlay layer, so they take ``highlight_column`` 

728 alone — and must be handed ``None`` under any other style, or "Mark border" 

729 would silently turn into text marking there (VIZ-23).""" 

730 if viz_settings.get("critical_span_style", "Mark text") != "Mark text": 

731 return None 

732 return viz_settings.get("highlight_column", "is_in_aspan")

803def _figure_input_key( 

804 words: pd.DataFrame, fixations: pd.DataFrame, build_kwargs: dict 

805) -> tuple: 

806 """Complete, hashable cache key for a single-trial scanpath figure. 

807 

808 Auto-derived from *all* build inputs — the frame fingerprints plus every 

809 kwarg — so changing any setting busts the cache. Deriving it mechanically 

810 (rather than listing settings by hand) means it can't drift out of sync with 

811 the figure builder and show a stale plot.""" 

812 parts = [ 

813 ("__words__", frame_fingerprint(words)), 

814 ("__fixations__", frame_fingerprint(fixations)), 

815 ] 

816 for k in sorted(build_kwargs): 

817 v = build_kwargs[k] 

818 if isinstance(v, pd.DataFrame): 

819 parts.append((k, frame_fingerprint(v))) 

820 elif isinstance(v, dict): 

821 parts.append((k, tuple(sorted((str(a), str(b)) for a, b in v.items())))) 

822 elif isinstance(v, (list, tuple)): 

823 parts.append((k, tuple(v))) 

824 else: 

825 try: 

826 hash(v) 

827 parts.append((k, v)) 

828 except TypeError: 

829 parts.append((k, str(v))) 

830 return tuple(parts) 

831 

832 

833@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Rendering scanpath…") 

834def _cached_scanpath_figure( 

835 _words: pd.DataFrame, 

836 _fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

837 _settings: FigureSettings, 

838 _raw_gaze: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

839 fig_key, 

840): 

841 """Build + cache a static single-trial scanpath figure. 

842 

843 Frames and settings are passed un-hashed; ``fig_key`` (from 

844 ``_figure_input_key``) is the cache key, so a rerun with the same trial and 

845 settings reuses the figure instead of rebuilding all its traces/shapes.""" 

846 return make_scanpath_figure( 

847 _words, _fixations, settings=_settings, raw_gaze=_raw_gaze 

848 )

850 

851_CMP_SORT_DEFAULT = "Same text, then same participant" 

852 

853 

854def _order_compare_options( 

855 options: list, 

856 choice: str, 

857 sort_keys: dict[str, pd.Series], 

858 *, 

859 descending: bool = False, 

860) -> list: 

861 """Sort comparison candidates with the main trial picker's vocabulary. 

862 

863 The comparison-specific default preserves ``build_comparison_options``'s 

864 relation priority: same text, then same participant, then everything else. 

865 Every other choice comes from ``utils.trial_sort_keys``, alongside its 

866 normal ``Trial ID`` default. 

867 """ 

868 if choice == _CMP_SORT_DEFAULT or len(options) < 2: 

869 return options 

870 key_series = None if choice == TRIAL_SORT_DEFAULT else sort_keys.get(choice) 

871 trial_ids = [str(option[1]) for option in options] 

872 ordered_ids = sort_trial_options( 

873 trial_ids, 

874 key_series, 

875 descending=descending if key_series is not None else False, 

876 ) 

877 rank = {trial_id: idx for idx, trial_id in enumerate(ordered_ids)} 

878 return sorted(options, key=lambda option: rank.get(str(option[1]), len(rank))) 

879

881def _render_compare_selector( 

882 combos: pd.DataFrame, 

883 selection_mode: str, 

884 selected_participant: str, 

885 selected_trial: str, 

886 selected_text: Optional[str], 

887 animate: bool = False, 

888 fixations_filtered: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

889 trial_words: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

890 words_filtered: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

891) -> tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]: 

892 """The compare-trial (B) selector, rendered above the chips (CMP-1). 

893 

894 Mirrors the main trial picker: a ``selectbox`` showing the trial id (+ 📄/👤 

895 markers) and a scrubbing ``select_slider`` showing ``"index/TOTAL · <trial 

896 id>"``, plus ◀ ▶ step buttons and a CMP-6 sort picker. The sort picker uses 

897 the main trial picker's generated choices; only its default differs, keeping 

898 same-text trials first, then same-participant trials, then the rest. The 

899 overlay layout + A/B-legend config live in the rail's **⚙️ Compare** popover 

900 (under the Compare toggle). Returns ``(participant, trial)``.""" 

901 options = build_comparison_options( 

902 combos, selection_mode, selected_participant, selected_trial, selected_text 

903 ) 

904 active_screen = None 

905 if ( 

906 trial_words is not None 

907 and not trial_words.empty 

908 and SCREEN_ID in trial_words.columns 

909 ): 

910 active_screen = str(trial_words[SCREEN_ID].iloc[0]) 

911 screen_source = ( 

912 fixations_filtered 

913 if fixations_filtered is not None 

914 and not fixations_filtered.empty 

915 and SCREEN_ID in fixations_filtered.columns 

916 else words_filtered 

917 ) 

918 if ( 

919 screen_source is None 

920 or screen_source.empty 

921 or SCREEN_ID not in screen_source.columns 

922 ): 

923 options = [] 

924 else: 

925 candidates_with_screen = set( 

926 map( 

927 tuple, 

928 screen_source.loc[ 

929 screen_source[SCREEN_ID].astype(str) == active_screen, 

930 ["participant_id", "trial_id"], 

931 ] 

932 .astype(str) 

933 .drop_duplicates() 

934 .to_numpy(), 

935 ) 

936 ) 

937 options = [ 

938 option 

939 for option in options 

940 if (str(option[0]), str(option[1])) in candidates_with_screen 

941 ] 

942 if ( 

943 fixations_filtered is not None 

944 and SCREEN_ID in fixations_filtered.columns 

945 ): 

946 fixations_filtered = fixations_filtered[ 

947 fixations_filtered[SCREEN_ID].astype(str) == active_screen 

948 ] 

949 if not options: 

950 st.info( 

951 "No other trials contain this screen." 

952 if active_screen 

953 else "No other trials available for comparison." 

954 ) 

955 return None, None 

956 

957 # CMP-6: candidate sorting is visually LAST in the picker row, after the 

958 # step buttons. It still executes before the selectbox/slider below, so a 

959 # change applies to their list on the same run. CMP-10 mirrors the main trial 

960 # picker: ◀ / ▶ / ⇅ share one right-packed `railbtn_*` pill cluster instead of 

961 # occupying three independent columns. UI-only — it never travels in a deep 

962 # link or saved config (same call as `share_identity_mode`, DATA-16/S3). 

963 n = len(options) 

964 sort_keys = trial_sort_keys( 

965 combos, 

966 "trial_id", 

967 words=words_filtered, 

968 fixations=fixations_filtered, 

969 ) 

970 sort_options = [_CMP_SORT_DEFAULT, TRIAL_SORT_DEFAULT, *sort_keys] 

971 sort_col = None 

972 if n > 1: 

973 sel_col, slider_col, trail_col = st.columns( 

974 [3, 5, 1.9], vertical_alignment="bottom" 

975 ) 

976 trail = trail_col.container(key="railbtn_single_compare_trail") 

977 # Create the children in display order, then fill the ordering popover 

978 # first because its result determines the option order used below. 

979 step_col = trail.container(key="railbtn_single_compare_step") 

980 sort_col = trail.container(key="railbtn_single_compare_sort") 

981 else: 

982 sel_col = st 

983 

984 sort_choice = _CMP_SORT_DEFAULT 

985 sort_desc = False 

986 if sort_col is not None: 

987 if st.session_state.get("single_compare_order") not in sort_options: 

988 st.session_state["single_compare_order"] = _CMP_SORT_DEFAULT 

989 with sort_col.popover("⇅", width="content", help="Sort the comparison trials"): 

990 sort_choice = st.selectbox( 

991 "Sort trials by", 

992 options=sort_options, 

993 key="single_compare_order", 

994 help="The default keeps related readings together: same text, then " 

995 "the same participant, then all remaining trials. Other choices " 

996 "match the main trial picker's sort menu.", 

997 ) 

998 sort_desc = st.checkbox( 

999 "Descending", 

1000 key="single_compare_sort_desc", 

1001 disabled=sort_choice in {_CMP_SORT_DEFAULT, TRIAL_SORT_DEFAULT}, 

1002 ) 

1003 options = _order_compare_options( 

1004 options, 

1005 sort_choice, 

1006 sort_keys, 

1007 descending=sort_desc, 

1008 ) 

1009 

1010 labels = [opt[2] for opt in options] 

1011 label_to_trial = {opt[2]: (opt[0], opt[1]) for opt in options} 

1012 label_to_id = {opt[2]: str(opt[1]) for opt in options} 

1013 

1014 sel_key = "single_compare_trial" 

1015 pos_key = "single_compare_pos" 

1016 current = st.session_state.get(sel_key) 

1017 if current not in labels: 

1018 current = labels[0] 

1019 st.session_state[sel_key] = current 

1020 

1021 if n > 1: 

1022 idx_of = {lbl: i for i, lbl in enumerate(labels)} 

1023 # Mirror the slider to the current selection before it renders. 

1024 st.session_state[pos_key] = current 

1025 

1026 def _on_compare_slider() -> None: 

1027 st.session_state[sel_key] = st.session_state[pos_key] 

1028 

1029 def _step_compare(delta: int) -> None: 

1030 try: 

1031 pos = labels.index(st.session_state.get(sel_key)) 

1032 except ValueError: 

1033 pos = 0 

1034 st.session_state[sel_key] = labels[max(0, min(pos + delta, n - 1))] 

1035 

1036 current_idx = labels.index(current) 

1037 

1038 picker_label = "**Compare To**" 

1039 if sort_choice not in {_CMP_SORT_DEFAULT, TRIAL_SORT_DEFAULT}: 

1040 picker_label += f" · by {sort_choice} {'↓' if sort_desc else '↑'}" 

1041 selected_compare_label = sel_col.selectbox( 

1042 picker_label, 

1043 options=labels, 

1044 key=sel_key, 

1045 help="Choose the second trial to compare against the selected trial. " 

1046 "📄 = same text · 👤 = same participant." 

1047 + (" Animated comparison overlays both on one clock." if animate else ""), 

1048 ) 

1049 if n > 1: 

1050 with slider_col: 

1051 st.select_slider( 

1052 "Compare position", 

1053 options=labels, 

1054 key=pos_key, 

1055 on_change=_on_compare_slider, 

1056 label_visibility="collapsed", 

1057 format_func=lambda v: ( 

1058 f"{idx_of.get(v, 0) + 1}/{n} · {label_to_id.get(v, v)}" 

1059 ), 

1060 help=f"Scrub through the {n} candidate trials.", 

1061 ) 

1062 step_col.button( 

1063 "◀", 

1064 key="single_compare_prev", 

1065 on_click=_step_compare, 

1066 args=(-1,), 

1067 disabled=current_idx == 0, 

1068 help="Previous candidate", 

1069 ) 

1070 step_col.button( 

1071 "▶", 

1072 key="single_compare_next", 

1073 on_click=_step_compare, 

1074 args=(1,), 

1075 disabled=current_idx == n - 1, 

1076 help="Next candidate", 

1077 ) 

1078 

1079 if selected_compare_label: 

1080 return label_to_trial[selected_compare_label] 

1081 return None, None 

1082 

1083 

1084_CRITICAL_SPAN_BG = "#FCE7F3" # light pink — critical-span words 

1085_DISTRACTOR_SPAN_BG = "#E5E7EB" # light grey — distractor-span words 

1086# These highlight backgrounds are always light (they mirror the light stimulus), 

1087# so pin a dark text color too — otherwise the inherited theme text color goes 

1088# light in dark mode and the highlighted text is unreadable (light-on-light). 

1089_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT_COLOR = "#212529" 

1090 

1091# Friendly labels + fixed span colours for the known OneStop stimulus/question 

1092# columns, so the OneStop experience is unchanged while the panel still works on 

1093# arbitrary datasets (unknown columns get a humanized name + a palette colour). 

1094_STIMULUS_FIELD_LABELS = { 

1095 "question": "Question", 

1096 "question_preview": "Question preview", 

1097 "selected_answer": "Selected answer", 

1098 "is_correct": "Correct", 

1099 "is_in_aspan": "Answer (critical) span", 

1100 "is_in_dspan": "Distractor span", 

1101} 

1102_KNOWN_SPAN_BG = {"is_in_aspan": _CRITICAL_SPAN_BG, "is_in_dspan": _DISTRACTOR_SPAN_BG} 

1103# Light backgrounds for any further detected span columns (cycled). 

1104_SPAN_BG_PALETTE = ["#FEF3C7", "#DBEAFE", "#DCFCE7", "#FAE8FF", "#FFE4E6"] 

1105# Substrings that mark a per-word boolean column as a highlightable span, and a 

1106# trial-level column as question/answer content. Dataset-agnostic by design. 

1107_SPAN_NAME_HINTS = ("span", "highlight", "critical", "target", "aoi_of_interest") 

1108_QA_NAME_HINTS = ("question", "answer", "correct", "response", "prompt") 

1109 

1110 

1111def _humanize_field(col: str) -> str: 

1112 """Friendly display label for a stimulus/question column.""" 

1113 return _STIMULUS_FIELD_LABELS.get(col, col.replace("_", " ").strip().capitalize()) 

1114 

1115 

1116def _is_boolish(series: pd.Series) -> bool: 

1117 """True when a column holds only boolean-like values (per-word span flags). 

1118 

1119 Accepts real booleans, numeric 0/1, and the string spellings ``True/False``. 

1120 Deliberately excludes string ``"0"``/``"1"`` so a string-typed id column that 

1121 happens to contain only ``"0"``/``"1"`` isn't mistaken for a span flag.""" 

1122 if pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(series): 

1123 return True 

1124 vals = set(series.dropna().unique()) 

1125 return bool(vals) and vals <= { 

1126 True, 

1127 False, 

1128 0, 

1129 1, 

1130 0.0, 

1131 1.0, 

1132 "True", 

1133 "False", 

1134 "true", 

1135 "false", 

1136 } 

1137 

1138 

1139def _detect_span_columns(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]: 

1140 """Per-word boolean columns that mark a highlightable span (generic). 

1141 

1142 Known OneStop spans (``is_in_aspan``/``is_in_dspan``) come first so they keep 

1143 their fixed colours; any further span-like boolean columns follow. 

1144 """ 

1145 detected = [ 

1146 c 

1147 for c in trial_words.columns 

1148 if any(h in c.lower() for h in _SPAN_NAME_HINTS) 

1149 and _is_boolish(trial_words[c]) 

1150 and bool(trial_words[c].fillna(False).astype(bool).any()) 

1151 ] 

1152 known = [c for c in ("is_in_aspan", "is_in_dspan") if c in detected] 

1153 rest = [c for c in detected if c not in known] 

1154 return known + rest 

1155 

1156 

1157def _detect_question_columns(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> list[str]: 

1158 """Trial-level columns holding question / answer content. 

1159 

1160 Matches columns whose name reads as question/answer/correct/… but excludes 

1161 span-named columns and **per-word-varying boolean** columns: a boolean that 

1162 differs across the trial's words (e.g. a per-word ``response`` mask) is 

1163 span-like data, not a trial-level field, and rendering its first value as 

1164 ``"Response: True"`` would be misleading. A *constant* boolean (e.g. 

1165 ``is_correct``) is a legitimate trial-level field and is kept. Also excludes 

1166 plain numeric columns (UX-32): a Q&A field is inherently text or boolean, so 

1167 an unrelated numeric column that merely matches a name hint — e.g. a 

1168 ``response_time_ms`` timing column on a generic upload — would otherwise 

1169 render as a bogus "Response time ms: 120" line. 

1170 """ 

1171 out = [] 

1172 for c in trial_words.columns: 

1173 lc = c.lower() 

1174 if c == "comprehension_questions": 

1175 continue # structured JSON, rendered by _render_comprehension_questions 

1176 if not any(h in lc for h in _QA_NAME_HINTS) or _is_boolish_span(c): 

1177 continue 

1178 col = trial_words[c] 

1179 boolish = _is_boolish(col) 

1180 if boolish and col.dropna().nunique() > 1: 

1181 continue # per-word-varying boolean → not a trial-level Q&A field 

1182 if not boolish and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(col): 

1183 continue # a timing/count/id column, not question/answer text 

1184 out.append(c) 

1185 return out 

1186 

1187 

1188#: Columns the Stimulus & questions field picker never offers (UX-32): the 

1189#: stimulus text itself, word geometry, and the identity columns the trial chips 

1190#: above the plot already carry. 

1191_STIMULUS_FIELD_EXCLUDE = frozenset( 

1192 { 

1193 "text", 

1194 "word_id", 

1195 "line_idx", 

1196 "x", 

1197 "y", 

1198 "width", 

1199 "height", 

1200 "participant_id", 

1201 "trial_id", 

1202 "text_id", 

1203 "comprehension_questions", 

1204 } 

1205) 

1206#: Session keys behind the picker. UI-only in the four-surface sense — they 

1207#: choose what a *panel* lists, not anything a figure renders, so there is nothing 

1208#: for the deep link / CLI / headless API to carry (see the note on UX-32). 

1209#: 

1210#: They are still **widget** keys, though, which the trial-chip picker they 

1211#: otherwise resemble is not (`controls.py` writes `trial_chip_fields` directly). 

1212#: That difference is load-bearing: Streamlit drops a widget's key at the end of 

1213#: any run in which the widget did not render, and this panel lives only in the 

1214#: Scanpath view — so one trip through Corpus Analysis would prune both keys, and 

1215#: the signature guard below (a plain key, which survives) would then never 

1216#: re-seed them. Hence `persist_state="session"` on both multiselects, the same 

1217#: rule as every `global_*` / `single_*` widget. 

1218_STIMULUS_SPAN_KEY = "stimulus_span_fields" 

1219_STIMULUS_QA_KEY = "stimulus_qa_fields" 

1220_STIMULUS_SIG_KEY = "_stimulus_fields_signature" 

1221 

1222 

1223@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

1224def _c_stimulus_field_candidates( 

1225 _trial_words: pd.DataFrame, cache_key: tuple 

1226) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]: 

1227 """Cached :func:`_stimulus_field_candidates` (house `_c_*` convention). 

1228 

1229 The scan is per-column `dropna().nunique()`, which on a wide schema (OneStop 

1230 ships ~60 columns) costs ~5 ms — small in isolation, but this panel renders 

1231 on *every* rerun of the Scanpath view regardless of which subtab is showing, 

1232 so uncached it was ~15× what the two name-hint detectors it replaced cost. 

1233 Keyed on the frame fingerprint like every other `_c_*` wrapper, so an edited 

1234 or re-uploaded corpus re-derives. 

1235 """ 

1236 return _stimulus_field_candidates(_trial_words) 

1237 

1238 

1239def _stimulus_field_candidates( 

1240 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

1241) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]: 

1242 """(span candidates, Q&A candidates) the picker may offer for this trial. 

1243 

1244 Wider than what :func:`_detect_span_columns` / :func:`_detect_question_columns` 

1245 pick automatically, and deliberately so — auto-detection has to be 

1246 conservative (it is what produced the `response_time_ms` false positive), but 

1247 once the user is choosing explicitly the right pool is *everything shaped 

1248 like* a span or a trial-level field, name hints aside. 

1249 

1250 The split is by shape, not by name, and it turns on whether a column *varies 

1251 across the trial's words*: a boolean that changes word to word marks a span, 

1252 a boolean that is constant is a trial-level fact (``is_correct``) and belongs 

1253 with the Q&A fields, exactly as :func:`_detect_question_columns` already 

1254 treats it. Constant non-boolean columns are Q&A candidates too, numeric ones 

1255 included — auto-detection refuses to guess at a numeric, but a deliberately 

1256 picked timing column is a legitimate thing to want on screen. 

1257 """ 

1258 spans, qa = [], [] 

1259 for col in trial_words.columns: 

1260 if col in _STIMULUS_FIELD_EXCLUDE: 

1261 continue 

1262 series = trial_words[col] 

1263 varies = series.dropna().nunique() > 1 

1264 if _is_boolish(series) and bool(series.fillna(False).astype(bool).any()): 

1265 (spans if varies else qa).append(col) 

1266 elif not varies: 

1267 qa.append(col) 

1268 return spans, qa 

1269 

1270 

1271def _stimulus_fields(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]: 

1272 """The span + Q&A columns to render, honouring the user's picks (UX-32). 

1273 

1274 Auto-detection stays the *default*; the picker only overrides it. The stored 

1275 choice is re-seeded whenever the dataset changes shape — switching to another 

1276 corpus should go back to what that corpus auto-detects, rather than leaving 

1277 the panel empty because none of the previous dataset's columns exist — but is 

1278 left alone otherwise, so stepping through trials doesn't undo a choice. 

1279 

1280 Returns ``(spans, qa)`` and also the option pools, so the picker beside it 

1281 doesn't scan the frame a second time. 

1282 """ 

1283 span_options, qa_options = _c_stimulus_field_candidates( 

1284 trial_words, frame_fingerprint(trial_words) 

1285 ) 

1286 # The signature is the *column set*, not the derived option pools. Those are 

1287 # computed from this trial's slice, so a trial whose critical span happens to 

1288 # be empty classifies that column differently — and keying the re-seed on 

1289 # them would silently reset the user's picks on that trial, which is the 

1290 # opposite of what the paragraph above promises. 

1291 signature = tuple(map(str, trial_words.columns)) 

1292 # Re-seed on a changed candidate pool *or* on a missing key. The second case 

1293 # should not happen — `persist_state="session"` is what keeps these alive 

1294 # while the panel is unmounted — but the signature is a plain key and would 

1295 # survive a pruning that took the widget keys with it, leaving the panel 

1296 # permanently blank with nothing to trigger a recovery. 

1297 if ( 

1298 st.session_state.get(_STIMULUS_SIG_KEY) != signature 

1299 or _STIMULUS_SPAN_KEY not in st.session_state 

1300 or _STIMULUS_QA_KEY not in st.session_state 

1301 ): 

1302 st.session_state[_STIMULUS_SIG_KEY] = signature 

1303 st.session_state[_STIMULUS_SPAN_KEY] = _detect_span_columns(trial_words) 

1304 st.session_state[_STIMULUS_QA_KEY] = _detect_question_columns(trial_words) 

1305 spans = [ 

1306 c for c in st.session_state.get(_STIMULUS_SPAN_KEY, []) if c in span_options 

1307 ] 

1308 qa = [c for c in st.session_state.get(_STIMULUS_QA_KEY, []) if c in qa_options] 

1309 return spans, qa, span_options, qa_options 

1310 

1311 

1312def _render_stimulus_field_picker(host, span_options, qa_options) -> None: 

1313 """The ⚙️ Fields popover: which columns this panel highlights and lists. 

1314 

1315 UX-32 asked whether this panel is still effectively OneStop-specific. The 

1316 honest answer was "generic when the column *names* cooperate" — a corpus 

1317 whose critical span is called `focus_region`, or whose question column is 

1318 `q_text`, got nothing. This is the escape hatch: name hints pick the 

1319 defaults, and anything they miss (or wrongly include) is one click away. 

1320 

1321 Takes the option pools rather than the frame: `_stimulus_fields` has already 

1322 derived them for this run, and re-deriving here scanned the words frame a 

1323 second time on every rerun. 

1324 """ 

1325 if not span_options and not qa_options: 

1326 return 

1327 with host.popover("⚙️ Fields", width="content"): 

1328 st.caption( 

1329 "Which of this dataset's columns the panel highlights and lists. " 

1330 "Detected by name to begin with — change them here when the naming " 

1331 "doesn't match, or to add a field the detection skipped." 

1332 ) 

1333 if span_options: 

1334 st.multiselect( 

1335 "Highlighted spans", 

1336 options=span_options, 

1337 key=_STIMULUS_SPAN_KEY, 

1338 persist_state="session", 

1339 help="Per-word true/false columns. Each selected one tints its " 

1340 "words in the stimulus text and gets a summary line below it.", 

1341 ) 

1342 if qa_options: 

1343 st.multiselect( 

1344 "Question & answer fields", 

1345 options=qa_options, 

1346 key=_STIMULUS_QA_KEY, 

1347 persist_state="session", 

1348 help="Trial-level columns (one value for the whole trial), " 

1349 "listed under the stimulus text.", 

1350 ) 

1351 

1352 

1353def _render_comprehension_questions(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> None: 

1354 """Render structured comprehension questions for the trial's stimulus. 

1355 

1356 Parses the ``comprehension_questions`` JSON column (MultiplEYE) into a list of 

1357 questions, each with the target (✓ reference answer) and distractors. The 

1358 corpus records no per-reader answer, so the target is shown as the key only — 

1359 not as a 'selected'/'correct' result. No-op when the column is absent or the 

1360 JSON is empty/malformed.""" 

1361 raw = _first_str(trial_words, "comprehension_questions") 

1362 if not raw: 

1363 return 

1364 try: 

1365 items = json.loads(raw) 

1366 except (ValueError, TypeError): 

1367 return 

1368 if not items: 

1369 return 

1370 st.markdown("**Comprehension questions**") 

1371 for i, q in enumerate(items, 1): 

1372 head = f"**Q{q.get('question_no') or i}**" 

1373 cond = (q.get("condition") or "").strip() 

1374 if cond and cond.lower() != "nan": 

1375 head += f" · _{cond}_" 

1376 st.markdown(f"{head}: {q.get('question', '')}") 

1377 options = [] 

1378 target = (q.get("target") or "").strip() 

1379 if target: 

1380 options.append(f"- ✓ {target}") 

1381 options += [f"- {d}" for d in q.get("distractors", []) if d] 

1382 if options: 

1383 st.markdown("\n".join(options)) 

1384 

1385 

1386def _is_boolish_span(col: str) -> bool: 

1387 """A name that reads as a span flag rather than a Q&A text field.""" 

1388 return any(h in col.lower() for h in _SPAN_NAME_HINTS) 

1389 

1390 

1391def _span_bg_for(col: str, idx: int) -> str: 

1392 """Background colour for a span column (fixed for OneStop, palette otherwise).""" 

1393 if col in _KNOWN_SPAN_BG: 

1394 return _KNOWN_SPAN_BG[col] 

1395 return _SPAN_BG_PALETTE[idx % len(_SPAN_BG_PALETTE)] 

1396 

1397 

1398def _ordered_words(trial_words: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame: 

1399 """Return trial_words sorted into reading order.""" 

1400 for col in ("word_id", "IA_ID"): 

1401 if col in trial_words.columns: 

1402 return trial_words.sort_values(col) 

1403 return trial_words 

1404 

1405 

1406def _render_paragraph_with_spans( 

1407 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, span_bg: Optional[dict] = None 

1408) -> None: 

1409 """Render the stimulus text with each detected span column highlighted. 

1410 

1411 ``span_bg`` maps a per-word boolean span column → its highlight background 

1412 (e.g. ``is_in_aspan`` → pink). When omitted, span columns are auto-detected. 

1413 Falls back to plain text when no span columns are present, so it works on any 

1414 dataset, not just OneStop.""" 

1415 if "text" not in trial_words.columns or trial_words.empty: 

1416 return 

1417 ordered = _ordered_words(trial_words) 

1418 if span_bg is None: 

1419 cols = _detect_span_columns(ordered) 

1420 span_bg = {c: _span_bg_for(c, i) for i, c in enumerate(cols)} 

1421 active = [c for c in span_bg if c in ordered.columns] 

1422 if not active: 

1423 st.write(" ".join(ordered["text"].astype(str).tolist())) 

1424 return 

1425 import html as _html 

1426 

1427 texts = ordered["text"].astype(str).tolist() 

1428 masks = {c: ordered[c].fillna(False).astype(bool).tolist() for c in active} 

1429 parts: list[str] = [] 

1430 for i, raw_word in enumerate(texts): 

1431 word = _html.escape(raw_word) 

1432 bg = "" 

1433 for col in active: # first matching span wins (known spans listed first) 

1434 if masks[col][i]: 

1435 bg = span_bg[col] 

1436 break 

1437 if bg: 

1438 parts.append( 

1439 f'<span style="background-color:{bg};color:{_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT_COLOR};' 

1440 f'padding:0 2px;border-radius:2px;">{word}</span>' 

1441 ) 

1442 else: 

1443 parts.append(word) 

1444 html_body = " ".join(parts) 

1445 st.markdown( 

1446 f'<div style="line-height:1.6;">{html_body}</div>', 

1447 unsafe_allow_html=True, 

1448 ) 

1449 

1450 

1451def _span_text(trial_words: pd.DataFrame, mask_col: str) -> str: 

1452 """Return the joined text of words where mask_col is True.""" 

1453 if mask_col not in trial_words.columns or "text" not in trial_words.columns: 

1454 return "" 

1455 ordered = _ordered_words(trial_words) 

1456 mask = ordered[mask_col].fillna(False).astype(bool) 

1457 return " ".join(ordered.loc[mask, "text"].astype(str).tolist()) 

1458 

1459 

1460def _first_str(df: pd.DataFrame, col: str) -> Optional[str]: 

1461 """First non-null value of ``col`` as a string, or None.""" 

1462 if col in df.columns: 

1463 vals = df[col].dropna() 

1464 if not vals.empty: 

1465 return str(vals.iloc[0]) 

1466 return None 

1467 

1468 

1469def _first_num(df: pd.DataFrame, col: str) -> Optional[float]: 

1470 """First non-null value of ``col`` as a float, or None when absent/empty.""" 

1471 if col in df.columns: 

1472 vals = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna() 

1473 if not vals.empty: 

1474 return float(vals.iloc[0]) 

1475 return None 

1476 

1477 

1478def _first_bool(df: pd.DataFrame, col: str) -> Optional[bool]: 

1479 """First non-null value of ``col`` as a bool, or None when absent/empty.""" 

1480 if col in df.columns: 

1481 vals = df[col].dropna() 

1482 if not vals.empty: 

1483 return bool(vals.iloc[0]) 

1484 return None 

1485 

1486 

1487def _span_fixated_note( 

1488 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

1489 trial_fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

1490 mask_col: str, 

1491) -> str: 

1492 """Inline HTML note: was the span fixated, and for how long? 

1493 

1494 Counts fixations falling inside any of the span's word boxes — a quick 

1495 "did the reader actually look at the answer?" check tying the scanpath to 

1496 comprehension. Returns "" when fixations or the span column are absent.""" 

1497 if ( 

1498 trial_fixations is None 

1499 or trial_fixations.empty 

1500 or mask_col not in trial_words.columns 

1501 ): 

1502 return "" 

1503 span_words = trial_words[trial_words[mask_col].fillna(False).astype(bool)] 

1504 if span_words.empty: 

1505 return "" 

1506 from scanpath_studio.measures import fixation_in_text_mask 

1507 

1508 mask = fixation_in_text_mask(trial_fixations, span_words) 

1509 n = int(mask.sum()) 

1510 if n == 0: 

1511 return ' <span style="color:#dc3545;">— not fixated</span>' 

1512 dwell = float(pd.to_numeric(trial_fixations.loc[mask, "duration_ms"]).sum()) 

1513 return f' <span style="color:#198754;">— {n} fixations, {dwell:.0f} ms</span>' 

1514 

1515 

1516def _render_trial_header( 

1517 participant: str, 

1518 trial_id: str, 

1519 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

1520 prefix: str = "Trial:", 

1521) -> None: 

1522 """Render the trial id header with participant + text id stacked below it. 

1523 

1524 The paragraph text / question / spans live in 

1525 `_render_paragraph_panel` so they can sit under the figure (single tab) 

1526 while the header stays in the side panel. 

1527 """ 

1528 lines = [f"**{prefix}** `{trial_id}`", f"Participant: `{participant}`"] 

1529 # The text/passage id may live under its canonical name or a pre-rename 

1530 # source name (unique_paragraph_id etc.), which can also double as a composite 

1531 # component — recognise all of them so the line reads "Text:" either way. 

1532 text_cols = ("unique_text_id", "text_id", "unique_paragraph_id", "paragraph_id") 

1533 text_id = None 

1534 for col in text_cols: 

1535 if col in trial_words.columns and not trial_words.empty: 

1536 value = trial_words[col].iloc[0] 

1537 if pd.notna(value): 

1538 text_id = value 

1539 break 

1540 if text_id is not None: 

1541 lines.append(f"Text: `{text_id}`") 

1542 # When the trial id was composed from several columns, surface its remaining 

1543 # parts on their own labeled lines too — the same way Participant and Text 

1544 # are shown — so the opaque `a_b_c` id is spelled out. Participant and the 

1545 # paragraph/text column are already covered above, so they're skipped. 

1546 composite_cols = st.session_state.get("_composite_trial_columns") or [] 

1547 already_shown = {"participant_id", *text_cols} 

1548 for col in composite_cols: 

1549 if col in already_shown or col not in trial_words.columns or trial_words.empty: 

1550 continue 

1551 value = trial_words[col].iloc[0] 

1552 if pd.notna(value): 

1553 lines.append(f"{col.replace('_', ' ').capitalize()}: `{value}`") 

1554 # Participant and Text sit on their own lines under the trial id (a markdown 

1555 # hard line break is two trailing spaces + newline). 

1556 st.markdown(" \n".join(lines)) 

1557 

1558 

1559def _render_paragraph_panel( 

1560 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

1561 *, 

1562 trial_fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame] = None, 

1563 expanded: bool = True, 

1564 bare: bool = False, 

1565) -> None: 

1566 """Render the stimulus-text + questions panel, generically. 

1567 

1568 Detects the dataset's text-span columns (any boolean per-word column whose 

1569 name reads as a span/highlight) and question/answer columns (any trial-level 

1570 column whose name reads as question/answer/correct), so it works on any 

1571 corpus — not just OneStop. Known OneStop columns keep their friendly labels 

1572 and span colours, so the OneStop view is unchanged. Each span is annotated 

1573 with whether it was fixated when ``trial_fixations`` is given. Skips silently 

1574 when no word text is available. ``bare=True`` drops the expander wrapper so 

1575 the panel can sit directly inside a subtab.""" 

1576 if "text" not in trial_words.columns or trial_words.empty: 

1577 return 

1578 # UX-32: the name-hint detection supplies the defaults; the ⚙️ Fields popover 

1579 # is what lets a corpus whose columns are named differently use the panel. 

1580 span_cols, qa_cols, span_options, qa_options = _stimulus_fields(trial_words) 

1581 span_bg = {c: _span_bg_for(c, i) for i, c in enumerate(span_cols)} 

1582 

1583 container = ( 

1584 st.container() 

1585 if bare 

1586 else st.expander("Stimulus & questions", expanded=expanded) 

1587 ) 

1588 with container: 

1589 text_col, picker_col = st.columns([9, 1.4], vertical_alignment="top") 

1590 _render_stimulus_field_picker(picker_col, span_options, qa_options) 

1591 with text_col: 

1592 _render_paragraph_with_spans(trial_words, span_bg) 

1593 

1594 # Breathing room between the stimulus text and the question block (generic 

1595 # Q&A fields and/or MultiplEYE's structured comprehension questions). 

1596 has_comprehension = bool(_first_str(trial_words, "comprehension_questions")) 

1597 if qa_cols or has_comprehension: 

1598 st.markdown("<div style='height:1.2rem'></div>", unsafe_allow_html=True) 

1599 

1600 # MultiplEYE structured comprehension questions (target + distractors). 

1601 _render_comprehension_questions(trial_words) 

1602 

1603 # Question / answer fields, generically. Keep OneStop's combined 

1604 # "selected X · ✓ correct" answer line when both columns are present. 

1605 question_cols = [c for c in qa_cols if "question" in c.lower()] 

1606 for col in question_cols: 

1607 val = _first_str(trial_words, col) 

1608 if val: 

1609 st.markdown(f"**{_humanize_field(col)}:** {val}") 

1610 

1611 rendered = set(question_cols) 

1612 if "selected_answer" in qa_cols and "is_correct" in qa_cols: 

1613 answer_val = _first_str(trial_words, "selected_answer") 

1614 correct = _first_bool(trial_words, "is_correct") 

1615 if answer_val or correct is not None: 

1616 bits = [] 

1617 if answer_val: 

1618 bits.append(f"selected **{answer_val}**") 

1619 if correct is not None: 

1620 bits.append(":green[✓ correct]" if correct else ":red[✗ incorrect]") 

1621 st.markdown("**Answer:** " + " · ".join(bits)) 

1622 rendered.update({"selected_answer", "is_correct"}) 

1623 

1624 # Any remaining detected answer/correct columns, rendered generically. 

1625 for col in qa_cols: 

1626 if col in rendered: 

1627 continue 

1628 bval = _first_bool(trial_words, col) if "correct" in col.lower() else None 

1629 if bval is not None: 

1630 mark = ":green[✓ yes]" if bval else ":red[✗ no]" 

1631 st.markdown(f"**{_humanize_field(col)}:** " + mark) 

1632 else: 

1633 val = _first_str(trial_words, col) 

1634 if val: 

1635 st.markdown(f"**{_humanize_field(col)}:** {val}") 

1636 

1637 # Each highlighted span's text + (optional) fixation note. 

1638 for col in span_cols: 

1639 span_str = _span_text(trial_words, col) 

1640 if not span_str: 

1641 continue 

1642 note = _span_fixated_note(trial_words, trial_fixations, col) 

1643 st.markdown( 

1644 _span_summary_html(col, span_str, span_bg[col], note), 

1645 unsafe_allow_html=True, 

1646 ) 

1647 

1648 

1649def _span_summary_html(col: str, span_str: str, bg: str, note: str) -> str: 

1650 """Markup for one "<span label>: <span text>" line in the stimulus panel. 

1651 

1652 Split out of ``_render_paragraph_panel`` so the escaping is testable without 

1653 a Streamlit runtime. Both data-derived values — the column name and the 

1654 stimulus text joined out of the words table — are HTML-escaped (S7): this 

1655 goes through ``unsafe_allow_html=True`` and Streamlit's markdown path runs 

1656 no sanitizer, so a corpus containing markup would otherwise inject it into 

1657 the page. ``note`` is tool-generated markup and ``bg`` comes from the fixed 

1658 ``_SPAN_BG_PALETTE``, so both stay raw. 

1659 """ 

1660 return ( 

1661 f'<span style="background-color:{bg};' 

1662 f'color:{_HIGHLIGHT_TEXT_COLOR};padding:0 4px;border-radius:2px;">' 

1663 f"<b>{html.escape(_humanize_field(col))}:</b></span> " 

1664 f"{html.escape(span_str)}{note}" 

1665 ) 

1666 

1667 

1668def _in_text_fixation_value( 

1669 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame 

1670) -> Optional[str]: 

1671 """Concise "in / total" count of fixations that landed inside a word box. 

1672 

1673 Replaces the old free-text caption ("All 154 fixations landed inside word 

1674 boxes.") with a compact value for the trial summary table. Returns None when 

1675 there's nothing to count.""" 

1676 if trial_words.empty or trial_fixations.empty: 

1677 return None 

1678 from scanpath_studio.measures import fixation_in_text_mask 

1679 

1680 mask = fixation_in_text_mask(trial_fixations, trial_words) 

1681 n_total = len(mask) 

1682 if n_total == 0: 

1683 return None 

1684 n_in = int(mask.sum()) 

1685 return f"{n_in} / {n_total}" 

1686 

1687 

1688def _summary_rows( 

1689 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame 

1690) -> list[dict]: 

1691 """Field/Value rows summarising a trial — totals + in-text fixation count. 

1692 

1693 Folded into the metadata table (formerly the three `st.metric` cards plus 

1694 the out-of-text caption), so a trial's headline numbers live in one place.""" 

1695 stats = compute_trial_stats(trial_words, trial_fixations) 

1696 rows = [ 

1697 { 

1698 "Field": "Total reading time (s)", 

1699 "Value": f"{stats['total_reading_time_s']:.1f}", 

1700 }, 

1701 {"Field": "Number of words", "Value": f"{stats['word_count']:,}"}, 

1702 {"Field": "Number of fixations", "Value": f"{stats['fixation_count']:,}"}, 

1703 ] 

1704 in_text = _in_text_fixation_value(trial_words, trial_fixations) 

1705 if in_text is not None: 

1706 rows.append({"Field": "Fixations in word boxes", "Value": in_text}) 

1707 return rows 

1708 

1709 

1710# Row-wise palette for the trial-metadata table. Picked light so the text 

1711# stays readable. `is_correct` keeps the row background neutral but tints 

1712# the value text green/red — adding a background there clashed with the 

1713# ✓ / ✗ color. 

1714_DIFFICULTY_COLORS = {"ele": "#d4edda", "adv": "#fff3cd"} 

1715_REPEAT_COLOR = "#cfe2ff" # light blue — clearly distinct from the Ele/Adv tints 

1716_PREVIEW_COLOR = "#DBEAFE" # light blue — Hunting/preview trials 

1717

1963def _collect_column_mapping() -> dict: 

1964 """The column-mapping selections from session_state, for config provenance. 

1965 

1966 The upload boxes share the ``col_map_*`` prefix (``state_prefix="col_map_fix"`` 

1967 etc.), so their ``file_uploader`` widgets land in this sweep too. Their value 

1968 is an ``UploadedFile`` (or list of them), which isn't JSON serializable and 

1969 isn't part of the column mapping — so the ``_upload`` widget keys are 

1970 excluded.""" 

1971 return { 

1972 k: st.session_state[k] 

1973 for k in sorted(st.session_state.keys()) 

1974 if isinstance(k, str) and k.startswith("col_map_") and not k.endswith("_upload") 

1975 }

1978def _render_save_restore_expander( 

1979 selected_participant: str, 

1980 selected_trial: str, 

1981 canvas_width: int, 

1982 canvas_height: int, 

1983 x_field: str, 

1984 y_field: str, 

1985 figure_settings: dict, 

1986 viz_settings: dict, 

1987 base_font_size: int, 

1988 trial_raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame, 

1989 *, 

1990 font_family: str, 

1991 slot=None, 

1992): 

1993 """Render the "💾 Save & restore" sidebar panel (DATA-9). 

1994 

1995 Merges the former Plot-configuration and Annotations panels into one: a 

1996 single JSON sidecar that captures the full figure configuration (layers, 

1997 colouring, sizing, text/highlighting, canvas, axes, trial selection) PLUS 

1998 every per-trial annotation, with a matching uploader to restore it all. So a 

1999 reviewer can save, share, and reload the exact state behind a figure. The 

2000 upload is *applied* in ``app._apply_uploaded_plot_config`` (it runs before 

2001 the widgets render). ``slot`` is a keyed sidebar container reserved by 

2002 ``app.main`` so the panel sits under the controls rather than after the tab. 

2003 """ 

2004 from datetime import datetime 

2005 

2006 from scanpath_studio import __version__, annotations 

2007 

2008 container = slot if slot is not None else st.sidebar 

2009 annotation_records = annotations.current_records() 

2010 # Provenance: which data source + how its columns were mapped + 

2011 # the app version + when it was exported, so a saved config records the full 

2012 # context behind the figure, not just the plot settings. 

2013 column_mapping = _collect_column_mapping() 

2014 # Per-scanpath comparison styling (cmp{idx}_* widget keys, seeded by 

2015 # controls._seed_compare_styles). Save the RAW values so they restore 1:1 — 

2016 # the saccade style stays the friendly label ("Solid"), not the resolved dash. 

2017 compare_styles = [ 

2018 { 

2019 "fix_color": st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_fix_color"), 

2020 "saccade_color": st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_color"), 

2021 "saccade_style": st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_style", "Solid"), 

2022 "saccade_width": float( 

2023 st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_saccade_width", DEFAULT_SACCADE_WIDTH) 

2024 ), 

2025 "marker_size_range": [ 

2026 int(s) 

2027 for s in st.session_state.get( 

2028 f"cmp{idx}_marker_size_range", DEFAULT_MARKER_SIZE_RANGE 

2029 ) 

2030 ], 

2031 "hollow": bool(st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_hollow", False)), 

2032 "opacity": float(st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_opacity", 1.0)), 

2033 # UX-31: the A/B legend label override ("" = the auto label). 

2034 "label_pattern": st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_label_pattern") or "", 

2035 } 

2036 for idx in range(2) 

2037 ] 

2038 plot_config = _build_studio_config( 

2039 selected_participant=selected_participant, 

2040 selected_trial=selected_trial, 

2041 canvas_width=canvas_width, 

2042 canvas_height=canvas_height, 

2043 x_field=x_field, 

2044 y_field=y_field, 

2045 figure_settings=figure_settings, 

2046 viz_settings=viz_settings, 

2047 base_font_size=base_font_size, 

2048 trial_raw_gaze=trial_raw_gaze, 

2049 font_family=font_family, 

2050 annotation_records=annotation_records, 

2051 column_mapping=column_mapping, 

2052 data_source=st.session_state.get("data_source_choice"), 

2053 app_version=__version__, 

2054 exported_at=datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds"), 

2055 compare_styles=compare_styles, 

2056 ) 

2057 open_requested = bool(st.session_state.pop("_open_save_restore", False)) 

2058 if open_requested: 

2059 with container: 

2060 embed_html_iframe( 

2061 """<script> 

2062 (function () { 

2063 const doc = window.parent.document; 

2064 let tries = 0; 

2065 (function openSidebar() { 

2066 const sidebar = doc.querySelector( 

2067 'section[data-testid="stSidebar"]'); 

2068 if (!sidebar) return; 

2069 if (sidebar.getAttribute("aria-expanded") !== "true") { 

2070 doc.querySelector( 

2071 'button[data-testid="stExpandSidebarButton"]' 

2072 )?.click(); 

2073 if (++tries < 20) setTimeout(openSidebar, 100); 

2074 return; 

2075 } 

2076 doc.querySelector(".st-key-tour_grp_save_restore") 

2077 ?.scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"}); 

2078 })(); 

2079 })(); 

2080 </script>""", 

2081 height=0, 

2082 ) 

2083 with container.expander( 

2084 "💾 Save & restore", 

2085 expanded=open_requested, 

2086 ): 

2087 n_anno = len(annotation_records) 

2088 st.caption( 

2089 "Save the full plot configuration **and** all annotations " 

2090 f"({n_anno} trial{'s' if n_anno != 1 else ''}) — plus the data " 

2091 "source and column mapping — to one JSON file, or restore them. " 

2092 "Everything that fits the loaded data is re-applied." 

2093 ) 

2094 st.download_button( 

2095 "⬇ Download (JSON)", 

2096 data=json.dumps(plot_config, indent=2), 

2097 # General filename — the config spans the whole session, not one 

2098 # trial. 

2099 file_name="scanpath_studio_config.json", 

2100 mime="application/json", 

2101 key="plot_config_download", 

2102 width="stretch", 

2103 ) 

2104 # S3: unlike the Share link — which now lets you drop the ids — this 

2105 # file always carries the selected participant/trial AND every note you 

2106 # have typed, for every annotated trial. Say so before it is mailed on. 

2107 st.caption( 

2108 "⚠️ The file names the selected participant and trial, and includes " 

2109 "the text of every annotation note you've written." 

2110 ) 

2111 st.file_uploader( 

2112 "Restore from JSON", 

2113 type=["json"], 

2114 key="plot_config_upload", 

2115 help="Re-apply settings + annotations from a file saved here earlier. " 

2116 "Anything that doesn't fit the loaded data is skipped.", 

2117 ) 

2118 skipped = st.session_state.get("_plot_config_skipped") 

2119 if skipped: 

2120 st.caption( 

2121 "⚠️ Not applied (no match in the current data): " 

2122 + ", ".join(skipped) 

2123 + "." 

2124 )

2127def _build_compare_meta( 

2128 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2129 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

2130 selected_participant: str, 

2131 selected_trial: str, 

2132 compare_participant: Optional[str], 

2133 compare_trial: Optional[str], 

2134 selected_screen: Optional[str] = None, 

2135) -> Optional[dict]: 

2136 """Build the second trial's words/fixations + column labels for the 

2137 side-by-side metadata table, or None when no comparison is active.""" 

2138 if compare_participant is None or compare_trial is None: 

2139 return None 

2140 compare_words = extract_trial(words_filtered, compare_participant, compare_trial) 

2141 compare_fix = extract_trial(fixations_filtered, compare_participant, compare_trial) 

2142 if selected_screen is not None: 

2143 if not compare_words.empty: 

2144 if SCREEN_ID not in compare_words.columns: 

2145 return None 

2146 compare_words = extract_part( 

2147 compare_words, compare_participant, compare_trial, selected_screen 

2148 ) 

2149 if not compare_fix.empty: 

2150 if SCREEN_ID not in compare_fix.columns: 

2151 return None 

2152 compare_fix = extract_part( 

2153 compare_fix, compare_participant, compare_trial, selected_screen 

2154 ) 

2155 if compare_words.empty and compare_fix.empty: 

2156 return None 

2157 # Short, distinct column headers: participant ids when comparing different 

2158 # participants (the common same-text case), else the trial ids — the long 

2159 # ids otherwise overflow the narrow panel. 

2160 if str(selected_participant) != str(compare_participant): 

2161 label_primary = str(selected_participant) 

2162 label_compare = str(compare_participant) 

2163 else: 

2164 label_primary = str(selected_trial) 

2165 label_compare = str(compare_trial) 

2166 return { 

2167 "words": compare_words, 

2168 "fixations": compare_fix, 

2169 "label_primary": label_primary, 

2170 "label_compare": label_compare, 

2171 "participant": compare_participant, 

2172 "trial": compare_trial, 

2173 } 

2174 

2175 

2176# Playback-speed options shared by the animation control. 

2177_ANIM_SPEED_OPTIONS = [0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0] 

2178_ANIM_SPEED_LABELS = [ 

2179 "×0.25", 

2180 "×0.5", 

2181 "×1", 

2182 "×1.5", 

2183 "×2", 

2184 "×2.5", 

2185 "×3", 

2186 "×4", 

2187 "×6", 

2188 "×8", 

2189] 

2190# Default playback speed — brisk enough for quick review (real-time ÷ 4) but 

2191# still legible; the Playback popover's speed slider slows it down (to ×0.25). 

2192_ANIM_DEFAULT_SPEED = 4.0 

2193_ANIM_QUALITY_PRESETS = { 

2194 # Fast enough for trial browsing and compact GIF/MP4 drafts. 

2195 "Coarse": (300, 120), 

2196 # High-fidelity review/export: noticeably smoother than the old 100 ms grid. 

2197 "Fine": (40, 900), 

2198} 

2199 

2200 

2201def _render_anim_info_box( 

2202 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

2203 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2204 words_b: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

2205 fixations_b: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

2206 selected_participant: str, 

2207 selected_trial: str, 

2208 compare_participant: Optional[str], 

2209 compare_trial: Optional[str], 

2210 playback_speed: float, 

2211 grid_step_ms: Optional[float] = None, 

2212 max_frames: Optional[int] = None, 

2213) -> float: 

2214 """Render the animation reading-time / playback info box (+ overlay caveats), 

2215 shown in the side panel under the Animate toggle. Returns the playback 

2216 duration in ms; the box deliberately omits a redundant fixation count.""" 

2217 dual = fixations_b is not None and not fixations_b.empty 

2218 summary = animation_timeline_summary( 

2219 [trial_fixations] + ([fixations_b] if dual else []), 

2220 playback_speed, 

2221 grid_step_ms=grid_step_ms, 

2222 max_frames=max_frames, 

2223 ) 

2224 reading_span_ms = summary["reading_span_ms"] 

2225 playback_ms = summary["playback_ms"] 

2226 if dual: 

2227 span_a = animation_playback_ms([trial_fixations], 1.0)[0] 

2228 span_b = animation_playback_ms([fixations_b], 1.0)[0] 

2229 st.info( 

2230 f"**A** reading time {span_a / 1000:.1f}s · **B** {span_b / 1000:.1f}s " 

2231 f"· Playback ×{playback_speed:g}: {playback_ms / 1000:.1f}s" 

2232 ) 

2233 if (compare_participant, compare_trial) == ( 

2234 selected_participant, 

2235 selected_trial, 

2236 ): 

2237 st.caption("⚠️ The second scanpath is the same trial as the first.") 

2238 else: 

2239 text_a = _trial_text_id(trial_words) 

2240 text_b = _trial_text_id(words_b) 

2241 if text_a is not None and text_b is not None and text_a != text_b: 

2242 st.warning( 

2243 "The two scanpaths are **different texts**, so the shared " 

2244 "word boxes don't line up — the spatial overlay isn't " 

2245 "meaningful. Best for two readings of the same paragraph." 

2246 ) 

2247 # VIZ-11 follow-up: state what the chosen grid actually produced. The cap 

2248 # coarsening the step used to be invisible, which is the whole reason the 

2249 # setting felt arbitrary. UX-30 folded it INTO the box below rather than 

2250 # leaving it as a second, detached caption at the foot of the popover: the 

2251 # frame count is part of the same "what will this replay be like?" answer. 

2252 grid = ( 

2253 f"**{summary['n_frames']}** frames · one every " 

2254 f"{summary['step_ms']:.0f} ms of reading" 

2255 ) 

2256 if summary["coarsened"]: 

2257 grid += ( 

2258 f" — coarsened from {summary['requested_step_ms']:.0f} ms to stay " 

2259 f"under the {max_frames or 360}-frame cap" 

2260 ) 

2261 if not dual: 

2262 st.info( 

2263 f"Reading time: {reading_span_ms / 1000:.1f}s · " 

2264 f"Playback at ×{playback_speed:g}: {playback_ms / 1000:.1f}s\n\n" 

2265 f"{grid}" 

2266 ) 

2267 else: 

2268 st.caption(grid) 

2269 return playback_ms

2272def _apply_preprocessing_caption(fig, participant, trial) -> None: 

2273 """Put PRE-15 cleaning provenance on-screen, in exports, and in metadata.""" 

2274 report = st.session_state.get("_preprocessing_report") 

2275 if not isinstance(report, pd.DataFrame) or report.empty: 

2276 return 

2277 row = report[ 

2278 (report["participant_id"].astype(str) == str(participant)) 

2279 & (report["trial_id"].astype(str) == str(trial)) 

2280 ] 

2281 if row.empty: 

2282 return 

2283 item = row.iloc[0] 

2284 text = ( 

2285 f"Preprocessing · {int(item.get('n_excluded', 0))}/" 

2286 f"{int(item.get('n_fixations_before', 0))} excluded " 

2287 f"({float(item.get('excluded_pct', 0)):.1%}) · " 

2288 f"{int(item.get('n_merged', 0))} merged" 

2289 ) 

2290 fig.add_annotation( 

2291 x=0, 

2292 y=0, 

2293 xref="paper", 

2294 yref="paper", 

2295 xanchor="left", 

2296 yanchor="bottom", 

2297 text=text, 

2298 showarrow=False, 

2299 font=dict(size=10, color="#5f6368"), 

2300 bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.82)", 

2301 borderpad=3, 

2302 ) 

2303 metadata = dict(fig.layout.meta or {}) 

2304 metadata["preprocessing"] = item.to_dict() 

2305 fig.update_layout(meta=metadata)

2308def _apply_title_caption( 

2309 fig, 

2310 viz_settings: dict, 

2311 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

2312 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

2313 participant: str, 

2314 trial: str, 

2315 combo_row: Optional[dict] = None, 

2316) -> None: 

2317 """EXP-5: stamp the rail's title/caption pattern onto ``fig``. 

2318 

2319 Reuses EXP-2's pattern language (`export.pattern_fields`/`render_pattern`/ 

2320 `annotate_figure`) but against the trial on screen, so all three render 

2321 paths — static, animation, compare — carry the same title/caption a bulk 

2322 export would produce for this trial. The rail control is the single source 

2323 of truth: `viz_settings["title_pattern"]`/`["caption_pattern"]` come from 

2324 `controls._collect_viz_settings`, and the Export panel's bulk section reads 

2325 the same two keys rather than keeping its own copy. 

2326 

2327 Reads straight from `viz_settings` (`.get()`, tolerant of a minimal dict) 

2328 rather than `_build_figure_settings`'s translated, all-keys-required shape 

2329 — the `{settings}` placeholder only needs a handful of them, and the 

2330 animation/comparison call sites don't otherwise need a full figure-builder 

2331 settings dict at all.""" 

2332 title_pattern = viz_settings.get("title_pattern") or "" 

2333 caption_pattern = viz_settings.get("caption_pattern") or "" 

2334 if not title_pattern and not caption_pattern: 

2335 return 

2336 settings_summary_input = { 

2337 "show_words": viz_settings.get("show_words", False), 

2338 "show_word_labels": viz_settings.get("show_labels", True), 

2339 "show_fixations": viz_settings.get("show_fix", True), 

2340 "show_saccades": viz_settings.get("show_saccades", True), 

2341 "show_heatmap": viz_settings.get("show_heatmap", False), 

2342 "color_by": viz_settings.get("color_by"), 

2343 "palette": viz_settings.get("palette"), 

2344 } 

2345 fields = pattern_fields( 

2346 participant, 

2347 trial, 

2348 trial_words, 

2349 trial_fixations, 

2350 settings_summary_input, 

2351 combo_row=combo_row, 

2352 ) 

2353 title = render_pattern(title_pattern, fields) if title_pattern else "" 

2354 caption = render_pattern(caption_pattern, fields) if caption_pattern else "" 

2355 annotate_figure(fig, title=title, caption=caption) 

2356 

2357 

2358#: The auto A/B legend label, written in the pattern language (UX-31). Kept as 

2359#: the pattern rather than the rendered text so the *same* string can be shown 

2360#: as the Label A/B placeholder — an empty box and this pattern produce the same 

2361#: label, which is exactly what the placeholder promises. 

2362DEFAULT_COMPARE_LABEL_PATTERN = "{participant_id} · {trial_id}" 

2363 

2364 

2365def _resolve_compare_label( 

2366 idx: int, 

2367 participant: Optional[str], 

2368 trial: Optional[str], 

2369 trial_words: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

2370 trial_fixations: Optional[pd.DataFrame], 

2371) -> str: 

2372 """UX-31: the A/B legend label for compare scanpath ``idx`` (0 or 1). 

2373 

2374 An explicit ``cmp{idx}_label_pattern`` (⚙️ Compare options popover, 

2375 EXP-2-style pattern + preview) overrides the plain ``participant · trial`` 

2376 default; empty (the common case) falls through to it unchanged.""" 

2377 default = f"{participant} · {trial}" 

2378 pattern = st.session_state.get(f"cmp{idx}_label_pattern") or "" 

2379 if not pattern or not participant or not trial: 

2380 return default 

2381 fields = pattern_fields( 

2382 participant, 

2383 trial, 

2384 trial_words if trial_words is not None else pd.DataFrame(), 

2385 trial_fixations if trial_fixations is not None else pd.DataFrame(), 

2386 {}, 

2387 ) 

2388 return render_pattern(pattern, fields) or default
