5073def render_per_group_tab( 

5074 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5075 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5076 *, 

5077 viz_settings: dict, 

5078 canvas_width: int, 

5079 canvas_height: int, 

5080 base_font_size: int, 

5081 font_family: str, 

5082 line_spacing: float = DEFAULT_LINE_SPACING, 

5083 scale_text_to_boxes: bool = True, 

5084) -> None: 

5085 """*What does this group look like?* — a cohort by the active filter. 

5086 

5087 The one-group case of the Groups tab (wrapped by ``render_groups_tab``).""" 

5088 st.caption( 

5089 "Define a **group** (split a field or build a filter set), then pool its " 

5090 "readers: distribution summaries, the cohort word profile, a per-reader " 

5091 "summary table, and the group's trend." 

5092 ) 

5093 if fixations_filtered.empty and words_filtered.empty: 

5094 st.info("No data after filtering.") 

5095 return 

5096 with st.expander("Group", expanded=True): 

5097 spec, label = _render_group_definition( 

5098 words_filtered, fixations_filtered, key="pgrp", two_groups=False 

5099 ) 

5100 _warn_word_only_group_fields(st, fixations_filtered, spec) 

5101 words_g = apply_group(words_filtered, spec or {}) 

5102 # One `apply_group` call, not two: it returns `frame[mask]`, a new full-size 

5103 # copy, so calling it again just to compute the cache key built a second 

5104 # corpus-sized frame that nothing else ever saw — and (since PERF-3) parked 

5105 # it in the fingerprint memo for the rest of the run. 

5106 fix_in = apply_group(fixations_filtered, spec or {}) 

5107 fix_g = _c_enrich_fix( 

5108 fix_in, 

5109 words_g, 

5110 frame_fingerprint(fix_in), 

5111 frame_fingerprint(words_g), 

5112 ) 

5113 n_readers = ( 

5114 fix_g["participant_id"].nunique() 

5115 if "participant_id" in getattr(fix_g, "columns", []) 

5116 else 0 

5117 ) 

5118 st.caption(f"**{label}** — {n_readers} reader(s), {len(fix_g)} fixations in scope.") 

5119 if (words_g is None or words_g.empty) and (fix_g is None or fix_g.empty): 

5120 st.info("This group is empty — widen the definition.") 

5121 return 

5122 view = st.selectbox( 

5123 "View", 

5124 ["Distributions", "Word profile", "Reader summary table", "Group trend"], 

5125 key="pgrp_view", 

5126 ) 

5127 fw = dict( 

5128 canvas_width=canvas_width, 

5129 base_font_size=base_font_size, 

5130 font_family=font_family, 

5131 ) 

5132 

5133 if view == "Distributions": # AN-14 

5134 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1]) 

5135 measure = _measure_picker(words_g, fix_g, key="pgrp_measure", host=c[0]) 

5136 if measure is None: 

5137 return 

5138 kind = c[1].selectbox("Plot", ["violin", "box"], key="pgrp14_kind") 

5139 normalize = _normalize_toggle(c[2], key="pgrp14_norm", disabled=measure.is_rate) 

5140 frame = fix_g if measure.frame == "fixations" else words_g 

5141 vals = measure_values(frame, measure, normalize=normalize) 

5142 _chart( 

5143 make_distribution_figure( 

5144 {label: vals}, 

5145 metric_label=measure.axis_label, 

5146 kind=kind, 

5147 colors=_corpus_series_colors(viz_settings), 

5148 **fw, 

5149 ) 

5150 ) 

5151 elif view == "Word profile": # AN-15 

5152 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1, 1]) 

5153 text_col, text_id = _text_picker(words_g, key="pgrp_text", host=c[0]) 

5154 if text_col is None or text_id is None: 

5155 st.info("No word-level data for this group.") 

5156 return 

5157 measure = _measure_picker( 

5158 words_g, fix_g, key="pgrp_measure", host=c[1], per_word_only=True 

5159 ) 

5160 if measure is None: 

5161 return 

5162 agg = c[2].selectbox( 

5163 "Aggregate", 

5164 _AGG_OPTIONS, 

5165 key="pgrp15_agg", 

5166 help="How each word's value is combined across the group's readers.", 

5167 ) 

5168 spread = c[3].selectbox("Spread", _SPREAD_OPTIONS, key="pgrp15_spread") 

5169 min_readers = _min_readers_input(st, key="pgrp15_min") 

5170 prof = _c_cohort_profile( 

5171 words_g, 

5172 text_col, 

5173 text_id, 

5174 measure.key, 

5175 agg, 

5176 spread, 

5177 False, 

5178 min_readers, 

5179 frame_fingerprint(words_g), 

5180 ) 

5181 prof = _apply_min_readers(st, prof, min_readers, key="pgrp15_note") 

5182 _chart( 

5183 make_word_profile_figure( 

5184 {label: prof}, 

5185 measure_label=measure.axis_label, 

5186 spread_label=spread, 

5187 colors=_corpus_series_colors(viz_settings), 

5188 **fw, 

5189 ) 

5190 ) 

5191 _download_tidy( 

5192 st, prof, name=f"group_profile_{measure.key}_{text_id}.csv", key="dl_pgrp15" 

5193 ) 

5194 elif view == "Reader summary table": # AN-16 

5195 table = _c_cohort_summary( 

5196 words_g, fix_g, frame_fingerprint(words_g), frame_fingerprint(fix_g) 

5197 ) 

5198 if table.empty: 

5199 st.info("No per-reader summaries for this group.") 

5200 return 

5201 trials = _c_trial_summary( 

5202 words_g, fix_g, frame_fingerprint(words_g), frame_fingerprint(fix_g) 

5203 ) 

5204 reader_tab, trial_tab = st.tabs(["Readers", "Trials"]) 

5205 with reader_tab: 

5206 st.dataframe(table, width="stretch", hide_index=True) 

5207 _download_tidy( 

5208 st, table, name="group_reader_summaries.csv", key="dl_pgrp16" 

5209 ) 

5210 with trial_tab: 

5211 st.dataframe(trials, width="stretch", hide_index=True) 

5212 _download_tidy( 

5213 st, trials, name="group_trial_summaries.csv", key="dl_pgrp16_trials" 

5214 ) 

5215 elif view == "Group trend": # AN-17 

5216 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1]) 

5217 measure = _measure_picker(words_g, fix_g, key="pgrp_measure", host=c[0]) 

5218 if measure is None: 

5219 return 

5220 agg = c[1].selectbox( 

5221 "Aggregate", 

5222 _AGG_OPTIONS, 

5223 key="pgrp17_agg", 

5224 help="How the measure is combined within each trial (across its words / fixations).", 

5225 ) 

5226 show_readers = c[2].checkbox( 

5227 "Per-reader behind", value=False, key="pgrp17_readers" 

5228 ) 

5229 frame = fix_g if measure.frame == "fixations" else words_g 

5230 sub = frame.copy() 

5231 sub["trial_index"] = derive_trial_index(sub) 

5232 df = metric_by_trial_index(sub, measure.column, agg=agg) 

5233 fig = make_trend_figure( 

5234 df, 

5235 x_col="trial_index", 

5236 y_label=measure.axis_label, 

5237 title=f"{measure.label} by trial index — {label}", 

5238 **fw, 

5239 ) 

5240 if show_readers: 

5241 per = per_participant_trend(sub, measure.column, agg=agg) 

5242 for rdr, grp in per.groupby("participant_id"): 

5243 grp = grp.sort_values("trial_index") 

5244 fig.add_scatter( 

5245 x=grp["trial_index"], 

5246 y=grp["value"], 

5247 mode="lines", 

5248 line=dict(color="rgba(150,150,150,0.35)", width=1), 

5249 name=str(rdr), 

5250 showlegend=False, 

5251 hoverinfo="skip", 

5252 ) 

5253 _chart(fig) 

5254 _download_tidy(st, df, name=f"group_trend_{measure.key}.csv", key="dl_pgrp17") 

5255

5257def render_group_comparison_tab( 

5258 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5259 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5260 *, 

5261 viz_settings: dict, 

5262 canvas_width: int, 

5263 canvas_height: int, 

5264 base_font_size: int, 

5265 font_family: str, 

5266 line_spacing: float = DEFAULT_LINE_SPACING, 

5267 scale_text_to_boxes: bool = True, 

5268) -> None: 

5269 """*How do two groups differ?* — two cohorts side by side (AN-18…22).""" 

5270 st.caption( 

5271 "Define **two groups** and compare them: overlaid distributions, the " 

5272 "per-word difference profile, paired summary bars, an effect size + test, " 

5273 "and a stacked two-group word heatmap. Exploratory — not pre-registered." 

5274 ) 

5275 if fixations_filtered.empty and words_filtered.empty: 

5276 st.info("No data after filtering.") 

5277 return 

5278 with st.expander("Groups A & B", expanded=True): 

5279 spec_a, spec_b, label_a, label_b = _render_group_definition( 

5280 words_filtered, fixations_filtered, key="cmp", two_groups=True 

5281 ) 

5282 spec_a = spec_a or {} 

5283 spec_b = spec_b or {} 

5284 _warn_word_only_group_fields(st, fixations_filtered, spec_a, spec_b) 

5285 na = apply_group(fixations_filtered, spec_a) 

5286 nb = apply_group(fixations_filtered, spec_b) 

5287 st.caption( 

5288 f"**{label_a}**: {na['participant_id'].nunique() if 'participant_id' in na else 0}" 

5289 f" reader(s) · **{label_b}**: " 

5290 f"{nb['participant_id'].nunique() if 'participant_id' in nb else 0} reader(s)." 

5291 ) 

5292 view = st.selectbox( 

5293 "View", 

5294 [ 

5295 "Overlaid distributions", 

5296 "Difference word profile", 

5297 "Paired summary bars", 

5298 "Effect size + test", 

5299 "Two-group word heatmap", 

5300 ], 

5301 key="cmp_view", 

5302 ) 

5303 fw = dict( 

5304 canvas_width=canvas_width, 

5305 base_font_size=base_font_size, 

5306 font_family=font_family, 

5307 ) 

5308 

5309 if view == "Overlaid distributions": # AN-18 

5310 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1]) 

5311 measure = _measure_picker( 

5312 words_filtered, fixations_filtered, key="cmp_measure", host=c[0] 

5313 ) 

5314 if measure is None: 

5315 return 

5316 kind = c[1].selectbox("Plot", ["violin", "box"], key="cmp18_kind") 

5317 normalize = _normalize_toggle(c[2], key="cmp18_norm", disabled=measure.is_rate) 

5318 frame = fixations_filtered if measure.frame == "fixations" else words_filtered 

5319 groups = two_group_values( 

5320 frame, 

5321 measure, 

5322 spec_a, 

5323 spec_b, 

5324 label_a=label_a, 

5325 label_b=label_b, 

5326 normalize=normalize, 

5327 ) 

5328 _chart( 

5329 make_distribution_figure( 

5330 groups, 

5331 metric_label=measure.axis_label, 

5332 kind=kind, 

5333 colors=_corpus_series_colors(viz_settings), 

5334 **fw, 

5335 ) 

5336 ) 

5337 elif view == "Difference word profile": # AN-19 

5338 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1, 1]) 

5339 text_col, text_id = _text_picker(words_filtered, key="cmp_text", host=c[0]) 

5340 if text_col is None or text_id is None: 

5341 st.info("No word-level data.") 

5342 return 

5343 measure = _measure_picker( 

5344 words_filtered, 

5345 fixations_filtered, 

5346 key="cmp_measure", 

5347 host=c[1], 

5348 per_word_only=True, 

5349 ) 

5350 if measure is None: 

5351 return 

5352 agg = c[2].selectbox( 

5353 "Aggregate", 

5354 _AGG_OPTIONS, 

5355 key="cmp19_agg", 

5356 help="How each word's value is combined across each group's readers, before A−B.", 

5357 ) 

5358 min_readers = _min_readers_input(c[3], key="cmp19_min", label="Min/grp") 

5359 diff = group_word_difference( 

5360 words_filtered, 

5361 text_col, 

5362 text_id, 

5363 measure, 

5364 spec_a, 

5365 spec_b, 

5366 agg=agg, 

5367 min_readers=min_readers, 

5368 ) 

5369 diff = _apply_min_readers(st, diff, min_readers, key="cmp19_note") 

5370 _chart( 

5371 make_difference_profile_figure( 

5372 diff, 

5373 measure_label=measure.axis_label, 

5374 label_a=label_a, 

5375 label_b=label_b, 

5376 colors=_corpus_series_colors(viz_settings), 

5377 **fw, 

5378 ) 

5379 ) 

5380 _download_tidy( 

5381 st, diff, name=f"difference_{measure.key}_{text_id}.csv", key="dl_cmp19" 

5382 ) 

5383 elif view == "Paired summary bars": # AN-20 

5384 all_measures = available_measures(words_filtered, fixations_filtered) 

5385 labels = {m.label: m.key for m in all_measures} 

5386 default = [ 

5387 m.label for m in all_measures if m.key in ("fix_dur", "sacc_amp", "tfd") 

5388 ] 

5389 chosen = st.multiselect( 

5390 "Measures", 

5391 list(labels), 

5392 default=default or list(labels)[:3], 

5393 key="cmp20_measures", 

5394 ) 

5395 c = st.columns(2) 

5396 agg = c[0].selectbox( 

5397 "Aggregate", 

5398 _AGG_OPTIONS, 

5399 key="cmp20_agg", 

5400 help="How each measure is combined across each group's readers.", 

5401 ) 

5402 spread = c[1].selectbox( 

5403 "Error bars", _SPREAD_OPTIONS, index=1, key="cmp20_spread" 

5404 ) 

5405 measures = [MEASURES[labels[m]] for m in chosen] 

5406 if not measures: 

5407 st.info("Pick at least one measure.") 

5408 return 

5409 df = paired_group_summary( 

5410 fixations_filtered, 

5411 measures, 

5412 spec_a, 

5413 spec_b, 

5414 agg=agg, 

5415 spread=spread, 

5416 label_a=label_a, 

5417 label_b=label_b, 

5418 words=words_filtered, 

5419 fixations=fixations_filtered, 

5420 ) 

5421 _chart(make_paired_bars_figure(df, **fw)) 

5422 _download_tidy(st, df, name="paired_group_means.csv", key="dl_cmp20") 

5423 elif view == "Effect size + test": # AN-21 

5424 c = st.columns([3, 2]) 

5425 measure = _measure_picker( 

5426 words_filtered, fixations_filtered, key="cmp_measure", host=c[0] 

5427 ) 

5428 if measure is None: 

5429 return 

5430 test = c[1].selectbox("Test", ["Mann–Whitney", "t-test"], key="cmp21_test") 

5431 frame = fixations_filtered if measure.frame == "fixations" else words_filtered 

5432 a = measure_values(apply_group(frame, spec_a), measure) 

5433 b = measure_values(apply_group(frame, spec_b), measure) 

5434 res = group_effect_size(a, b, test=test) 

5435 cols = st.columns(4) 

5436 cols[0].metric( 

5437 f"{label_a} mean", 

5438 f"{res['mean_a']:.2f}", 

5439 delta=f"n={res['n_a']}", 

5440 delta_color="off", 

5441 ) 

5442 cols[1].metric( 

5443 f"{label_b} mean", 

5444 f"{res['mean_b']:.2f}", 

5445 delta=f"n={res['n_b']}", 

5446 delta_color="off", 

5447 ) 

5448 cols[2].metric("Mean difference", f"{res['mean_diff']:.2f}") 

5449 cols[3].metric("Cohen's d", f"{res['cohen_d']:.3f}") 

5450 p = res.get("p_value") 

5451 p_txt = ( 

5452 "—" 

5453 if p is None or (isinstance(p, float) and np.isnan(p)) 

5454 else ("< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}") 

5455 ) 

5456 st.markdown( 

5457 f"**{test}** — statistic = {res['statistic']:.3g}, p = {p_txt}. " 

5458 f"_Exploratory, not pre-registered._" 

5459 ) 

5460 elif view == "Two-group word heatmap": # AN-22 

5461 c = st.columns([3, 1, 1]) 

5462 text_col, text_id = _text_picker(words_filtered, key="cmp_text", host=c[0]) 

5463 if text_col is None or text_id is None: 

5464 st.info("No word-level data.") 

5465 return 

5466 measure = _measure_picker( 

5467 words_filtered, 

5468 fixations_filtered, 

5469 key="cmp_measure", 

5470 host=c[1], 

5471 per_word_only=True, 

5472 ) 

5473 if measure is None: 

5474 return 

5475 agg = c[2].selectbox( 

5476 "Aggregate", 

5477 _AGG_OPTIONS, 

5478 key="cmp22_agg", 

5479 help="How each word's value is combined across each group's readers.", 

5480 ) 

5481 long = two_group_word_profiles( 

5482 words_filtered, 

5483 text_col, 

5484 text_id, 

5485 measure, 

5486 spec_a, 

5487 spec_b, 

5488 agg=agg, 

5489 label_a=label_a, 

5490 label_b=label_b, 

5491 ) 

5492 _chart( 

5493 make_word_matrix_heatmap( 

5494 long, 

5495 row_col="group", 

5496 measure_label=measure.axis_label, 

5497 row_order=[label_a, label_b], 

5498 **fw, 

5499 ) 

5500 ) 

5501 _download_tidy( 

5502 st, long, name=f"two_group_{measure.key}_{text_id}.csv", key="dl_cmp22" 

5503 )

5511def _best_model_indices(table: pd.DataFrame) -> dict: 

5512 """Row index of the best-scoring model per *real* metric column. 

5513 

5514 Min when the metric is lower-is-better, max otherwise. Placeholder metrics 

5515 (``fn is None``) and all-NaN columns are skipped, so they get no entry. 

5516 """ 

5517 best_index: dict[str, object] = {} 

5518 for metric in METRICS: 

5519 if metric.fn is None or metric.label not in table.columns: 

5520 continue 

5521 col = pd.to_numeric(table[metric.label], errors="coerce") 

5522 if col.notna().any(): 

5523 best_index[metric.label] = ( 

5524 col.idxmin() if metric.lower_is_better else col.idxmax() 

5525 ) 

5526 return best_index 

5527 

5528 

5529def _metric_arrow(metric) -> str: 

5530 """Direction arrow for a metric header: ↓ when lower is more similar, ↑ when 

5531 higher is.""" 

5532 return "↓" if metric.lower_is_better else "↑" 

5533 

5534 

5535def _style_similarity_table(table: pd.DataFrame): 

5536 """Format the similarity table and highlight the best model per metric. 

5537 

5538 Each metric header gets a direction arrow (↓ lower-is-better / ↑ 

5539 higher-is-better) so it's clear which way means *more similar*. Placeholder 

5540 metrics (all-NaN columns) render as "—"; for each real metric the 

5541 best-scoring model's cell is tinted green. 

5542 """ 

5543 # Header relabelling: "NLD" -> "NLD ↓", etc. Keep the original-label 

5544 # best-index, then translate its keys to the arrowed headers for highlighting. 

5545 header_map = { 

5546 m.label: f"{m.label} {_metric_arrow(m)}" 

5547 for m in METRICS 

5548 if m.label in table.columns 

5549 } 

5550 best_index = _best_model_indices(table) 

5551 best_by_header = { 

5552 header_map[label]: idx 

5553 for label, idx in best_index.items() 

5554 if label in header_map 

5555 } 

5556 

5557 display = table.copy() 

5558 for label in header_map: 

5559 display[label] = display[label].map( 

5560 lambda v: f"{v:.3f}" if pd.notna(v) else "—" 

5561 ) 

5562 display = display.rename(columns=header_map) 

5563 

5564 def _highlight(row: pd.Series) -> list[str]: 

5565 styles = [] 

5566 for col in display.columns: 

5567 style = "" 

5568 if col in best_by_header and row.name == best_by_header[col]: 

5569 style = "background-color: #d4edda; font-weight: 600;" 

5570 styles.append(style) 

5571 return styles 

5572 

5573 return display.style.apply(_highlight, axis=1) 

5574 

5575 

5576def render_alignment_comparison_tab( 

5577 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

5578 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

5579 *, 

5580 canvas_width: int, 

5581 canvas_height: int, 

5582 base_font_size: int, 

5583 font_family: str, 

5584 viz_settings: dict, 

5585 line_spacing: float, 

5586 scale_text_to_boxes: bool, 

5587 selected_participant, 

5588 selected_trial, 

5589) -> None: 

5590 """PRE-3 · Side-by-side grid comparing the vertical drift-correction algorithms. 

5591 

5592 One panel per algorithm (plus the uncorrected original), each snapping 

5593 fixations to their assigned text line and colouring by line, so a researcher 

5594 can see how the ten Carr et al. (2021) algorithms assign fixations for this 

5595 trial. The in-place version (a single algorithm applied on the main plot) 

5596 lives in the Fixations popover; this subtab is the all-at-once comparison. 

5597 """ 

5598 from scanpath_studio.measures import assign_fixation_lines 

5599 

5600 st.caption( 

5601 "Each panel snaps fixations to the text line assigned by a vertical " 

5602 "drift-correction algorithm " 

5603 "([Carr et al., 2021](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-021-01554-0)) and " 

5604 "colours them by line. Pick one to apply on the main plot via " 

5605 "**Fixations ⚙️ → Drift correction**." 

5606 ) 

5607 with st.expander("Algorithm citations", expanded=False): 

5608 st.markdown( 

5609 "Primary source: Carr et al. (2021), *Behavior Research Methods*, " 

5610 "[doi:10.3758/s13428-021-01554-0](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-021-01554-0)." 

5611 ) 

5612 for method in alignment.ALGORITHMS: 

5613 st.markdown(f"- **{method}** — {alignment.METHOD_CITATIONS[method]}") 

5614 

5615 if trial_fixations.empty or trial_words.empty: 

5616 st.info("No fixations / word boxes for this trial to align.") 

5617 return 

5618 

5619 # Building the 11-panel grid (each a true-scale Plotly figure) is expensive, 

5620 # and Streamlit renders every subtab on each rerun — so gate it behind a 

5621 # toggle the user opts into. The toggle state persists, so it stays on while 

5622 # browsing trials once enabled. 

5623 if not st.toggle( 

5624 "Show comparison grid", 

5625 key="align_grid_show", 

5626 help="Build a side-by-side grid comparing all ten algorithms for this " 

5627 "trial. Off by default — building eleven figures is slow.", 

5628 ): 

5629 st.caption( 

5630 "Turn on **Show comparison grid** to compare all ten algorithms side " 

5631 "by side, or apply one directly via **Fixations ⚙️ → Drift " 

5632 "correction** on the main plot." 

5633 ) 

5634 return 

5635 

5636 # The text lines we snap to (shared with the per-algorithm panels). Fewer than 

5637 # two lines → nothing to correct, so just show the original. 

5638 line_centers = alignment._line_centers(trial_words) 

5639 single_line = len(line_centers) < 2 

5640 if single_line: 

5641 st.info( 

5642 "This trial has only one text line — there is no vertical drift to " 

5643 "correct. Showing the original scanpath." 

5644 ) 

5645 

5646 ctrl_cols = st.columns([1, 1]) 

5647 with ctrl_cols[0]: 

5648 n_cols = st.slider( 

5649 "Panels per row", 

5650 min_value=2, 

5651 max_value=3, 

5652 value=2, 

5653 key="align_grid_ncols", 

5654 ) 

5655 with ctrl_cols[1]: 

5656 show_connectors = st.checkbox( 

5657 "Show drift connectors", 

5658 key="align_grid_connectors", 

5659 help="Draw a faint line from each fixation's original position to its " 

5660 "corrected (snapped) position in every panel.", 

5661 ) 

5662 

5663 # Clean, comparable spatial view: pin axes to x/y, drop the heatmap / raw gaze 

5664 # / labels / order numbers (illegible at grid scale), colour by line. 

5665 base_settings = _build_figure_settings(viz_settings, False) 

5666 base_settings["raw_gaze"] = None 

5667 base_settings["line_spacing"] = line_spacing 

5668 base_settings["scale_text_to_boxes"] = scale_text_to_boxes 

5669 panel_settings = { 

5670 **base_settings, 

5671 "show_heatmap": False, 

5672 "show_raw_gaze": False, 

5673 "show_word_labels": False, 

5674 "show_order": False, 

5675 "fixation_flags": None, 

5676 "color_by_line": True, 

5677 } 

5678 

5679 def _make_fig(fix: pd.DataFrame, *, connectors=None): 

5680 kwargs = dict(panel_settings) 

5681 if connectors is not None: 

5682 kwargs["show_connectors"] = True 

5683 kwargs["connector_y"] = tuple(pd.to_numeric(connectors, errors="coerce")) 

5684 return make_scanpath_figure( 

5685 trial_words, 

5686 fix, 

5687 canvas_width=int(canvas_width), 

5688 canvas_height=int(canvas_height), 

5689 base_font_size=int(base_font_size), 

5690 font_family=font_family, 

5691 x_field="x", 

5692 y_field="y", 

5693 **kwargs, 

5694 ) 

5695 

5696 # Naive baseline (nearest-line) to count how many fixations each algorithm 

5697 # moves relative to the current "color by line" behaviour. 

5698 baseline = assign_fixation_lines(trial_fixations, trial_words) 

5699 _, sensitivity_report = alignment.correction_sensitivity( 

5700 trial_fixations, trial_words 

5701 ) 

5702 st.dataframe( 

5703 sensitivity_report, 

5704 hide_index=True, 

5705 width="stretch", 

5706 column_config={ 

5707 "average_y_correction": st.column_config.NumberColumn(format="%.1f px"), 

5708 "max_y_correction": st.column_config.NumberColumn(format="%.1f px"), 

5709 }, 

5710 ) 

5711 st.caption( 

5712 "Sensitivity QA: large mean corrections or disagreement between methods " 

5713 "identify trials whose measures deserve manual review." 

5714 ) 

5715 

5716 # Build the panel list: original first, then the 10 algorithms (skipped when 

5717 # there is only a single line, where they would all be no-ops). 

5718 panels = [("Original (uncorrected)", None)] 

5719 if not single_line: 

5720 panels += [(a.title(), a) for a in alignment.ALGORITHMS] 

5721 

5722 # Estimate a uniform cell height so panels line up (mirrors the multiple- 

5723 # comparison grid). 

5724 probe = _make_fig(trial_fixations) 

5725 fig_w = float(probe.layout.width or 900) 

5726 fig_h = float(probe.layout.height or 600) 

5727 aspect = fig_h / fig_w if fig_w else 0.5 

5728 assumed_col_px = max(200, int(780 / max(1, n_cols))) 

5729 cell_h = max(150, int(assumed_col_px * aspect) + 16) 

5730 

5731 for start in range(0, len(panels), n_cols): 

5732 row = panels[start : start + n_cols] 

5733 grid_cols = st.columns(n_cols) 

5734 for cell, (label, method) in zip(grid_cols, row): 

5735 with cell: 

5736 if method is None: 

5737 st.caption(f"**{label}** · {len(trial_fixations)} fix") 

5738 fig = _make_fig(trial_fixations) 

5739 else: 

5740 corrected, line = alignment.correct( 

5741 trial_fixations, trial_words, method=method 

5742 ) 

5743 n_lines_used = int(line.dropna().nunique()) 

5744 moved = ( 

5745 (line.fillna(-1) != baseline.fillna(-1)).sum() 

5746 if len(baseline) == len(line) 

5747 else 0 

5748 ) 

5749 st.caption( 

5750 f"**{label}** · {n_lines_used} lines · {int(moved)} moved · " 

5751 f"mean |Δy| {corrected['y_correction'].abs().mean():.1f}px" 

5752 ) 

5753 fig = _make_fig( 

5754 corrected, 

5755 connectors=trial_fixations["y"] if show_connectors else None, 

5756 ) 

5757 moved_mask = corrected["y_correction"].abs().gt(0.5) 

5758 if moved_mask.any(): 

5759 import plotly.graph_objects as go 

5760 

5761 fig.add_trace( 

5762 go.Scatter( 

5763 x=corrected.loc[moved_mask, "x"], 

5764 y=corrected.loc[moved_mask, "y"], 

5765 mode="markers", 

5766 marker=dict( 

5767 symbol="circle-open", 

5768 size=16, 

5769 color="#d62728", 

5770 line=dict(width=2, color="#d62728"), 

5771 ), 

5772 name="Moved by correction", 

5773 customdata=corrected.loc[ 

5774 moved_mask, "y_correction" 

5775 ].to_numpy(), 

5776 hovertemplate="Moved Δy %{customdata:.1f}px<extra></extra>", 

5777 ) 

5778 ) 

5779 _render_true_scale_chart( 

5780 fig, 

5781 key=f"align_{label.replace(' ', '_').replace('(', '').replace(')', '')}", 

5782 max_height=cell_h, 

5783 ) 

5784 

5785 

5786# Per-fixation continuous quantities can't group scanpaths into generations, so 

5787# they're never offered as a generation identifier. 

5788_GEN_COL_EXCLUDE = { 

5789 "x", 

5790 "y", 

5791 "duration_ms", 

5792 "timestamp_ms", 

5793 "saccade_amplitude", 

5794 "order_in_trial", 

5795 "first_fix_x", 

5796 "first_fix_y", 

5797 "noise_flag", 

5798 # Per-fixation identifiers — grouping by these would make one "generation" 

5799 # per fixation / word, not per scanpath, so they're never generation columns. 

5800 "word_id", 

5801 "fixation_id", 

5802} 

5803# The grid shows at most this many generation panels (readability). When more 

5804# than this exist they're ranked by similarity to the selected scanpath and the 

5805# *closest* ones are shown — never an arbitrary label-sorted subset. 

5806_GEN_MAX_PANELS = 24 

5807# Score at most this many generations (bounds the NLD cost for a high-cardinality 

5808# column like participant_id on a big corpus). A safety budget above the grid cap 

5809# so the "most similar" ranking still sees more candidates than it displays. 

5810_GEN_MAX_SCORE = 60 

5811 

5812 

5813def _generation_column_options(fixations: pd.DataFrame) -> list: 

5814 """Columns that can identify the different generations of a scanpath. 

5815 

5816 A generation column splits a text's scanpaths into comparable variants (a 

5817 model / condition / reading id), so we offer the non-coordinate columns that 

5818 actually vary and rank the most generation-like first (a name hit, then the 

5819 reader / trial ids, then everything else).""" 

5820 if fixations is None or fixations.empty: 

5821 return [] 

5822 hints = ( 

5823 "generation", 

5824 "model", 

5825 "source", 

5826 "system", 

5827 "variant", 

5828 "condition", 

5829 "method", 

5830 "decoding", 

5831 "run", 

5832 "sample", 

5833 ) 

5834 cols = [] 

5835 for c in fixations.columns: 

5836 if c in _GEN_COL_EXCLUDE: 

5837 continue 

5838 try: 

5839 if fixations[c].nunique(dropna=True) >= 2: 

5840 cols.append(c) 

5841 except TypeError: 

5842 # A column holding unhashable values (e.g. a list / JSON column like 

5843 # MultiplEYE's `comprehension_questions`) can't group scanpaths. 

5844 continue 

5845 

5846 def _rank(col: str) -> tuple: 

5847 low = col.lower() 

5848 if any(h in low for h in hints): 

5849 return (0, col) 

5850 if col in ("participant_id", "trial_id"): 

5851 return (1, col) 

5852 return (2, col) 

5853 

5854 return sorted(cols, key=_rank) 

5855 

5856 

5857def _n_readings(fix: pd.DataFrame) -> int: 

5858 """How many distinct (participant, trial) readings a generation group holds. 

5859 

5860 CMP-5: a high-level grouping column (a condition, a regime) can lump several 

5861 readings into one "generation"; the panels say so instead of drawing the 

5862 concatenation as if it were one scanpath.""" 

5863 if {"participant_id", "trial_id"} <= set(fix.columns): 

5864 return int(len(fix[["participant_id", "trial_id"]].drop_duplicates())) 

5865 return 1 

5866 

5867 

5868def _panel_identity(fix: pd.DataFrame, gen_col: str, k: int) -> str: 

5869 """CMP-5 panel suffix naming the trial(s) behind a generation panel. 

5870 

5871 ``k`` is the group's reading count (from ``_n_readings``, computed once per 

5872 rerun by the tab). A single-reading group is labelled with its 

5873 ``participant · trial`` identity (unless the grouping column IS one of 

5874 those, where the group label already says it); a multi-reading group is 

5875 flagged with its reading count.""" 

5876 if k > 1: 

5877 return f" · ⚠️ {k} readings" 

5878 if gen_col in ("participant_id", "trial_id"): 

5879 return "" 

5880 if {"participant_id", "trial_id"} <= set(fix.columns) and not fix.empty: 

5881 row = fix.iloc[0] 

5882 return f" · {row['participant_id']} · {row['trial_id']}" 

5883 return "" 

5884 

5885 

5886def _collect_generations( 

5887 fixations_pool: pd.DataFrame, 

5888 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

5889 gen_col: str, 

5890 selected_participant, 

5891 selected_trial, 

5892) -> tuple: 

5893 """Same-text scanpaths grouped by ``gen_col``, minus the selected trial. 

5894 

5895 Scopes the pool to the selected trial's **text** so only variants of the SAME 

5896 text are compared (using the best-available text identifier — normalized 

5897 fixations use ``text_id`` / ``unique_text_id``, not always ``paragraph_id``), 

5898 drops the selected (participant, trial) so it isn't scored against itself, 

5899 groups the rest by ``gen_col`` → ``{label: fixations}``, and caps the panel 

5900 count. Returns ``(generations, n_total)`` where ``n_total`` is the count 

5901 before the cap.""" 

5902 if gen_col not in fixations_pool.columns or fixations_pool.empty: 

5903 return {}, 0 

5904 pool = fixations_pool 

5905 if SCREEN_ID in trial_fixations.columns and not trial_fixations.empty: 

5906 if SCREEN_ID not in pool.columns: 

5907 return {}, 0 

5908 active_screen = str(trial_fixations[SCREEN_ID].iloc[0]) 

5909 pool = pool[pool[SCREEN_ID].astype(str) == active_screen] 

5910 # Match the canonical text-column priority used elsewhere (utils / pickers): 

5911 # the first present on the fixations frame identifies the text. 

5912 text_col = next( 

5913 ( 

5914 c 

5915 for c in ( 

5916 "unique_text_id", 

5917 "text_id", 

5918 "unique_paragraph_id", 

5919 "paragraph_id", 

5920 ) 

5921 if c in pool.columns 

5922 ), 

5923 None, 

5924 ) 

5925 if text_col is not None and not trial_fixations.empty: 

5926 text_val = trial_fixations[text_col].iloc[0] 

5927 if pd.notna(text_val): 

5928 pool = pool[pool[text_col] == text_val] 

5929 if {"participant_id", "trial_id"} <= set(pool.columns): 

5930 pool = pool[ 

5931 ~( 

5932 (pool["participant_id"] == selected_participant) 

5933 & (pool["trial_id"] == selected_trial) 

5934 ) 

5935 ] 

5936 generations: dict = {} 

5937 for value, group in pool.groupby(gen_col, dropna=True): 

5938 if group.empty: 

5939 continue 

5940 label = str(value) 

5941 # Two distinct values that stringify the same (e.g. int 1 and str "1" in 

5942 # a mixed object column) must not collapse — disambiguate so neither group 

5943 # is silently lost and n_total stays accurate. 

5944 if label in generations: 

5945 label = f"{label} ({value!r})" 

5946 generations[label] = group 

5947 n_total = len(generations) 

5948 # Cap the SCORING budget only (the grid/ranking cut to _GEN_MAX_PANELS by 

5949 # similarity happens in the tab, after scoring). Sorted for determinism. 

5950 ordered = dict(sorted(generations.items())[:_GEN_MAX_SCORE]) 

5951 return ordered, n_total 

5952 

5953 

5954def render_multiple_comparison_tab( 

5955 trial_words: pd.DataFrame, 

5956 trial_fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

5957 words_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5958 fixations_filtered: pd.DataFrame, 

5959 *, 

5960 selected_participant: str, 

5961 selected_trial: str, 

5962 canvas_width: int, 

5963 canvas_height: int, 

5964 base_font_size: int, 

5965 font_family: str, 

5966 viz_settings: dict, 

5967 line_spacing: float = DEFAULT_LINE_SPACING, 

5968 scale_text_to_boxes: bool = True, 

5969) -> None: 

5970 """Render the **Comparisons** subtab. 

5971 

5972 Compares the scanpath for the *selected* trial (from the main trial picker) 

5973 against other scanpaths of the same text — grouped by a user-chosen column (a 

5974 reading regime, repeated-reading id, model generation, …) — and scores each 

5975 against the selected reading (NLD plus placeholder metrics). The selection 

5976 comes from the main scanpath picker; there's no separate picker here (ENG-8). 

5977 """ 

5978 st.caption( 

5979 "Compare the **selected** scanpath (from the main trial picker above) with " 

5980 "other scanpaths of the same text — grouped by a column you choose (a " 

5981 "reading regime, repeated-reading id, model generation, …) — and score how " 

5982 "close each is to the selected reading." 

5983 ) 

5984 if trial_words.empty or trial_fixations.empty: 

5985 st.info( 

5986 "Comparisons needs a **words + fixations** table for the selected " 

5987 "trial — pick a trial with fixations in the main picker above." 

5988 ) 

5989 return 

5990 

5991 gen_cols = _generation_column_options(fixations_filtered) 

5992 if not gen_cols: 

5993 st.info( 

5994 "No column in the fixations table can distinguish several scanpaths of " 

5995 "the same text. Load data whose fixations carry a regime / condition / " 

5996 "reading-id column (or use `participant_id` / `trial_id`) to compare " 

5997 "several scanpaths over the same text here." 

5998 ) 

5999 return 

6000 

6001 col_side, col_main = st.columns([3, 7], gap="medium") 

6002 

6003 with col_side: 

6004 gen_col = st.selectbox( 

6005 "Comparison column", 

6006 options=gen_cols, 

6007 key="multi_gen_col", 

6008 help="Which column identifies the scanpaths to compare. Each distinct " 

6009 "value — over the SAME text as the selected trial — becomes one " 

6010 "comparison scanpath, scored against the selected reading.", 

6011 ) 

6012 n_cols = st.slider( 

6013 "Grid columns", 

6014 min_value=1, 

6015 max_value=4, 

6016 value=3, 

6017 key="multi_n_cols", 

6018 help="Columns in the comparison grid (rows fill automatically).", 

6019 ) 

6020 

6021 generations, n_total = _collect_generations( 

6022 fixations_filtered, 

6023 trial_fixations, 

6024 gen_col, 

6025 selected_participant, 

6026 selected_trial, 

6027 ) 

6028 if not generations: 

6029 with col_main: 

6030 st.info( 

6031 f"No other scanpaths of this text found for **{gen_col}** in the " 

6032 "current filter — only the selected scanpath matches. Widen the " 

6033 "trial filters or pick a different comparison column." 

6034 ) 

6035 return 

6036 # More scanpaths of this text exist than we score (very high-cardinality 

6037 # column); the ones we do score are ranked by similarity below. 

6038 scored_capped = n_total > len(generations) 

6039 

6040 with col_side: 

6041 # ENG-8: no local fixation-index slider (it duplicated the main rail's 

6042 # Fixations → index-range control) and no stimulus-text panel (the 

6043 # top-level "Stimulus & questions" subtab already shows it). The grid and 

6044 # table score the full readings; the rail control still windows the main 

6045 # plot above. 

6046 _render_trial_header( 

6047 selected_participant, 

6048 selected_trial, 

6049 trial_words, 

6050 prefix="Selected scanpath:", 

6051 ) 

6052 if scored_capped: 

6053 # CMP-5: say exactly what was dropped and how the kept ones were 

6054 # chosen — the cap keeps the first _GEN_MAX_SCORE in label order. 

6055 st.caption( 

6056 f"{n_total} scanpaths of this text — more than the scoring " 

6057 f"budget. Scoring the first {len(generations)} by " 

6058 f"**{gen_col}** label order; the rest are not shown." 

6059 ) 

6060 

6061 # Reuse the user's viz toggles but force a clean, comparable spatial view: the 

6062 # grid is inherently spatial, and a generation frame may lack the selected 

6063 # trial's extra columns, so pin axes to x/y, colour by duration_ms (present in 

6064 # every frame), and turn off heatmap / raw gaze / by-line / flags (they group 

6065 # by (participant_id, trial_id) against trial_words and would mis-render). 

6066 base_settings = _build_figure_settings(viz_settings, False) 

6067 base_settings["raw_gaze"] = None 

6068 base_settings["line_spacing"] = line_spacing 

6069 base_settings["scale_text_to_boxes"] = scale_text_to_boxes 

6070 real_settings = { 

6071 **base_settings, 

6072 "show_heatmap": False, 

6073 "show_raw_gaze": False, 

6074 "color_by": "duration_ms", 

6075 "color_by_line": False, 

6076 "fixation_flags": None, 

6077 } 

6078 panel_settings = {**real_settings, "show_word_labels": False, "show_order": False} 

6079 

6080 def _make_fig(fix: pd.DataFrame, settings: dict): 

6081 return make_scanpath_figure( 

6082 trial_words, 

6083 fix, 

6084 canvas_width=int(canvas_width), 

6085 canvas_height=int(canvas_height), 

6086 base_font_size=int(base_font_size), 

6087 font_family=font_family, 

6088 x_field="x", 

6089 y_field="y", 

6090 **settings, 

6091 ) 

6092 

6093 # The full readings feed the spatial figures, the snapshot table, and the 

6094 # convergence plots (ENG-8 removed the local fixation-index window). 

6095 sliced_real = trial_fixations 

6096 sliced_gens = generations 

6097 

6098 with col_main: 

6099 # CMP-5: name the reference prominently — it comes from the main trial 

6100 # picker on a different part of the page, so the tab must say which 

6101 # reading everything below is scored against. 

6102 st.markdown( 

6103 f"#### Selected scanpath — `{selected_participant}` · `{selected_trial}`" 

6104 ) 

6105 real_fig = _make_fig(sliced_real, real_settings) 

6106 _render_true_scale_chart(real_fig, key="multi_real") 

6107 

6108 # Score every collected generation against the selected scanpath. The 

6109 # per-generation NLD annotates each grid panel and orders both the grid and 

6110 # the table; the full table is shown beneath the grid. 

6111 table = compute_similarity_table(sliced_real, sliced_gens, trial_words) 

6112 nld_by_gen = ( 

6113 dict(zip(table["Model"], table["NLD"])) if "NLD" in table.columns else {} 

6114 ) 

6115 

6116 # Rank by similarity (lowest NLD = most similar; unscored/NaN last) and show 

6117 # the closest _GEN_MAX_PANELS in the grid — never an arbitrary label subset. 

6118 ranked = sorted( 

6119 sliced_gens, 

6120 key=lambda n: ( 

6121 pd.isna(nld_by_gen.get(n)), 

6122 nld_by_gen.get(n) if pd.notna(nld_by_gen.get(n)) else 0.0, 

6123 ), 

6124 ) 

6125 grid_names = ranked[:_GEN_MAX_PANELS] 

6126 grid_capped = len(sliced_gens) > _GEN_MAX_PANELS 

6127 

6128 st.markdown("#### Other scanpaths") 

6129 # CMP-5: state the grouping and the ranking rule in the tab itself — 

6130 # one panel per value of the chosen column, ranked by similarity. 

6131 rank_note = ( 

6132 f"One panel per **{gen_col}** value over the same text, ranked by " 

6133 "NLD similarity to the selected scanpath above (most similar first)." 

6134 ) 

6135 if grid_capped: 

6136 rank_note += ( 

6137 f" Showing the **{_GEN_MAX_PANELS} most similar** of " 

6138 f"{len(sliced_gens)} scored." 

6139 ) 

6140 st.caption(rank_note) 

6141 # CMP-5: a value that groups several readings draws them concatenated in 

6142 # one panel — flag it rather than letting it pass as one scanpath. The 

6143 # counts are computed once per rerun and reused by the panel captions. 

6144 reading_counts = {name: _n_readings(g) for name, g in sliced_gens.items()} 

6145 if any(k > 1 for k in reading_counts.values()): 

6146 st.caption( 

6147 "⚠️ A value grouping **several readings** (marked on its panel) " 

6148 "shows them concatenated and scores them as one sequence — pick " 

6149 "a finer comparison column (e.g. `participant_id`) to see them " 

6150 "separately." 

6151 ) 

6152 # Estimate a uniform cell height from the figure aspect + column count so 

6153 # panels line up and don't leave a tall whitespace band below each. 

6154 fig_w = float(real_fig.layout.width or 900) 

6155 fig_h = float(real_fig.layout.height or 600) 

6156 aspect = fig_h / fig_w if fig_w else 0.5 

6157 assumed_col_px = max(360, int(1200 / max(1, n_cols))) 

6158 cell_h = max(280, int(assumed_col_px * aspect) + 24) 

6159 

6160 names = grid_names 

6161 for start in range(0, len(names), n_cols): 

6162 row_names = names[start : start + n_cols] 

6163 grid_cols = st.columns(n_cols) 

6164 for offset, (cell, name) in enumerate(zip(grid_cols, row_names)): 

6165 with cell: 

6166 fix = sliced_gens[name] 

6167 nld = nld_by_gen.get(name) 

6168 # CMP-5: every panel names its group value AND the trial it 

6169 # is (or its reading count when the value lumps several). 

6170 identity = _panel_identity( 

6171 fix, gen_col, reading_counts.get(name, 1) 

6172 ) 

6173 if nld is not None and pd.notna(nld): 

6174 st.caption( 

6175 f"**{name}** · NLD {nld:.2f} · {len(fix)} fix{identity}" 

6176 ) 

6177 else: 

6178 st.caption(f"**{name}** · {len(fix)} fix{identity}") 

6179 # Key on the absolute panel index (dict order is stable), so two 

6180 # labels differing only by spaces can't collide on the iframe key. 

6181 _render_true_scale_chart( 

6182 _make_fig(fix, panel_settings), 

6183 key=f"multi_gen_{start + offset}", 

6184 max_height=cell_h, 

6185 ) 

6186 

6187 st.markdown("#### Similarity to the selected scanpath") 

6188 st.dataframe( 

6189 _style_similarity_table(table.rename(columns={"Model": "Generation"})), 

6190 hide_index=True, 

6191 width="stretch", 

6192 ) 

6193 

6194 # Cumulative NLD convergence over the full scanpaths. Memoized on the 

6195 # selection + comparison column + set + a content fingerprint so unrelated 

6196 # reruns don't recompute the curves. 

6197 st.markdown("#### Metric convergence") 

6198 st.caption( 

6199 "NLD between the selected scanpath and each comparison scanpath, " 

6200 "computed cumulatively over the first *k* fixations (left) and the " 

6201 "first *t* seconds of reading (right). Lower = more similar; computed " 

6202 "on the full reading." 

6203 ) 

6204 if trial_fixations.empty: 

6205 fix_fingerprint: tuple = (0,) 

6206 else: 

6207 fix_fingerprint = ( 

6208 len(trial_fixations), 

6209 len(trial_words), 

6210 round(float(pd.to_numeric(trial_fixations["x"]).sum()), 3), 

6211 round(float(pd.to_numeric(trial_fixations["y"]).sum()), 3), 

6212 round(float(pd.to_numeric(trial_fixations["duration_ms"]).sum()), 3), 

6213 ) 

6214 # Convergence covers the grid subset (the shown, most-similar generations), 

6215 # so it matches the grid and stays bounded on a high-cardinality column. 

6216 conv_gens = {name: generations[name] for name in grid_names} 

6217 conv_key = ( 

6218 str(selected_participant), 

6219 str(selected_trial), 

6220 str(gen_col), 

6221 tuple(sorted(conv_gens.keys())), 

6222 fix_fingerprint, 

6223 ) 

6224 if st.session_state.get("_multi_conv_key") != conv_key: 

6225 st.session_state["_multi_conv_key"] = conv_key 

6226 st.session_state["_multi_conv_fix"] = { 

6227 name: nld_by_fixation_index(trial_fixations, g, trial_words) 

6228 for name, g in conv_gens.items() 

6229 } 

6230 st.session_state["_multi_conv_time"] = { 

6231 name: nld_by_time(trial_fixations, g, trial_words) 

6232 for name, g in conv_gens.items() 

6233 } 

6234 fix_curves = st.session_state["_multi_conv_fix"] 

6235 time_curves = st.session_state["_multi_conv_time"] 

6236 

6237 conv_cols = st.columns(2) 

6238 with conv_cols[0]: 

6239 fig_idx = make_metric_convergence_figure( 

6240 fix_curves, 

6241 x_title="Cumulative fixation index", 

6242 y_title="NLD", 

6243 title="NLD vs fixation index", 

6244 canvas_width=520, 

6245 base_font_size=int(base_font_size), 

6246 font_family=font_family, 

6247 ) 

6248 st.plotly_chart(fig_idx, width="stretch", config={"responsive": True}) 

6249 with conv_cols[1]: 

6250 fig_time = make_metric_convergence_figure( 

6251 time_curves, 

6252 x_title="Elapsed reading time (s)", 

6253 y_title="NLD", 

6254 title="NLD vs time", 

6255 canvas_width=520, 

6256 base_font_size=int(base_font_size), 

6257 font_family=font_family, 

6258 ) 

6259 st.plotly_chart(fig_time, width="stretch", config={"responsive": True}) 

6260

6267def _render_raw_table(df: pd.DataFrame, caption: Optional[str] = None) -> None: 

6268 """Render one of the raw Data Inspection tables, whole. 

6269 

6270 ``lazy=True`` (ENG-36 — Streamlit 1.61) replaced a hand-rolled pager: a 

6271 **Page** number box, a `.iloc` slice and a "rows 1,001 – 2,000 of 4,300,000" 

6272 caption. Streamlit now keeps the frame on the app server and streams only the 

6273 rows in view, which is both less code and a better table — the user scrolls 

6274 and sorts across the *whole* corpus instead of one thousand rows at a time, 

6275 and a rerun no longer ships the visible page to the browser again. Passing it 

6276 explicitly rather than leaving the default: the default only kicks in above 

6277 150 000 rows, and these are exactly the frames worth streaming well below 

6278 that. 

6279 

6280 There is deliberately no download button here: these are the *raw* frames, 

6281 which carry passthrough columns like ``image_path`` that hold an absolute 

6282 local path. Bulk export is the supported way out, and it strips those at its 

6283 single chokepoint (``export.strip_local_paths``). 

6284 """ 

6285 st.dataframe(df, hide_index=True, width="stretch", lazy=True) 

6286 if caption: 

6287 st.caption(caption) 

6288

6321@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Building stimuli list…") 

6322def _build_stimuli_table_cached(_words: pd.DataFrame, cache_key) -> pd.DataFrame: 

6323 """One row per Text ID, with the stimulus text reconstructed from its words. 

6324 

6325 The word table carries one row per word per text (and, for per-participant 

6326 tables, repeated once per reader). We collapse identical word rows across 

6327 participants, then join each text's words in reading order (line, then word 

6328 id) into a single passage string. Cached on a cheap content fingerprint of 

6329 the words frame (the frame itself is passed un-hashed via the underscore 

6330 arg) so a rerun that doesn't change the data reuses the result. 

6331 """ 

6332 empty = pd.DataFrame(columns=["Text ID", "# Words", "Text"]) 

6333 if _words.empty or "text_id" not in _words.columns or "text" not in _words.columns: 

6334 return empty 

6335 

6336 cols = [ 

6337 c 

6338 for c in ("text_id", "unique_text_id", "word_id", "line_idx", "text") 

6339 if c in _words.columns 

6340 ] 

6341 sub = _words[cols].copy() 

6342 sub = sub.dropna(subset=["text_id"]) 

6343 if sub.empty: 

6344 return empty 

6345 

6346 # Collapse identical word rows coming from multiple participants (stimulus 

6347 # AoIs are shared by every reader; per-participant tables repeat them). 

6348 if "word_id" in sub.columns: 

6349 sub = sub.drop_duplicates(subset=["text_id", "word_id"]) 

6350 else: 

6351 sub = sub.drop_duplicates() 

6352 

6353 sort_cols = ["text_id"] + [c for c in ("line_idx", "word_id") if c in sub.columns] 

6354 sub = sub.sort_values(sort_cols, kind="stable") 

6355 

6356 # Only surface unique_text_id as its own column when it actually differs 

6357 # from text_id (after the unique_paragraph_id fallback they're identical). 

6358 has_unique = "unique_text_id" in sub.columns and not ( 

6359 sub["unique_text_id"].astype(str).eq(sub["text_id"].astype(str)).all() 

6360 ) 

6361 

6362 rows = [] 

6363 for text_id, grp in sub.groupby("text_id", sort=False): 

6364 words_list = [w for w in grp["text"].astype(str).tolist() if w and w != "nan"] 

6365 row = { 

6366 "Text ID": text_id, 

6367 "# Words": len(words_list), 

6368 "Text": " ".join(words_list), 

6369 } 

6370 if has_unique: 

6371 uniques = grp["unique_text_id"].dropna().astype(str).unique().tolist() 

6372 row["Unique Text ID"] = ", ".join(uniques) 

6373 rows.append(row) 

6374 

6375 result = pd.DataFrame(rows) 

6376 ordered = ["Text ID"] 

6377 if has_unique: 

6378 ordered.append("Unique Text ID") 

6379 ordered += ["# Words", "Text"] 

6380 return result[[c for c in ordered if c in result.columns]] 

6381 

6382 

6383def render_stimuli_tab(words_filtered: pd.DataFrame) -> None: 

6384 """Render the stimuli subtab — one reconstructed passage per Text ID.""" 

6385 st.subheader("Stimuli") 

6386 if words_filtered.empty: 

6387 st.info("No word data available after filtering.") 

6388 return 

6389 stimuli = _build_stimuli_table_cached( 

6390 words_filtered, cache_key=frame_fingerprint(words_filtered) 

6391 ) 

6392 if stimuli.empty: 

6393 st.info( 

6394 "No stimulus text could be reconstructed — check the Word text and " 

6395 "Text ID column mappings." 

6396 ) 

6397 return 

6398 _render_raw_table(stimuli)

6401def _render_data_provenance() -> None: 

6402 """Show a 'source / cohort / date / file mtime' banner above the Raw Data 

6403 sub-tabs so reviewers can verify which OneStop export they're looking at. 

6404 

6405 Only renders when ONESTOP_DATA_DIR is set (i.e. OneStop server bundle is 

6406 the active data source). For uploads / bundled demo, falls through silently. 

6407 """ 

6408 from datetime import datetime 

6409 

6410 from .data import onestop_data_provenance 

6411 

6412 # Honour the deep-link participant so the per-pid shard's mtime is shown. 

6413 pid = st.session_state.get("single_participant") 

6414 info = onestop_data_provenance(participant=pid) 

6415 if not info: 

6416 return 

6417 

6418 def _fmt_mtime(ts): 

6419 return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") if ts else "—" 

6420 

6421 cols = st.columns(4) 

6422 cols[0].metric("Source", info.get("source", "—")) 

6423 cols[1].metric("Cohort", info.get("cohort", "—")) 

6424 cols[2].metric("Date", info.get("date", "—")) 

6425 cols[3].metric("File mtime", _fmt_mtime(info.get("ia_shard_mtime"))) 

6426 

6427 with st.expander("Data provenance — full paths"): 

6428 st.caption(f"`ONESTOP_DATA_DIR = {info.get('data_dir', '?')}`") 

6429 st.caption( 

6430 f"loaded from: **{info.get('loaded_from', '?')}**" 

6431 + (f" · participant `{pid}`" if pid else "") 

6432 ) 

6433 if "ia_shard" in info: 

6434 st.caption( 

6435 f"IA file: `{info['ia_shard']}` " 

6436 f"· mtime `{_fmt_mtime(info.get('ia_shard_mtime'))}`" 

6437 ) 

6438 if "fix_shard" in info: 

6439 st.caption( 

6440 f"Fixations file: `{info['fix_shard']}` " 

6441 f"· mtime `{_fmt_mtime(info.get('fix_shard_mtime'))}`" 

6442 )

6470@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Computing dataset statistics…") 

6471def _dataset_statistics( 

6472 _words: pd.DataFrame, 

6473 _fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

6474 _raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame, 

6475 cache_key, 

6476) -> dict: 

6477 """Compute the Data Inspection tab's summary aggregates. 

6478 

6479 Pure function of the (filtered) frames, cached on a cheap fingerprint so the 

6480 full-corpus ``groupby``/``unique``/``mean`` scans don't re-run on every rerun 

6481 (e.g. when the user merely selects a different trial).""" 

6482 participant_ids = set(_words["participant_id"].unique()) | set( 

6483 _fixations["participant_id"].unique() 

6484 ) 

6485 trial_ids = set(_words["trial_id"].unique()) | set(_fixations["trial_id"].unique()) 

6486 if "participant_id" in _raw_gaze.columns: 

6487 participant_ids |= set(_raw_gaze["participant_id"].unique()) 

6488 trial_ids |= set(_raw_gaze["trial_id"].unique()) 

6489 text_col = "unique_text_id" if "unique_text_id" in _words.columns else "text_id" 

6490 text_ids = set(_words[text_col].unique()) if text_col in _words.columns else set() 

6491 

6492 trial_source = _fixations if not _fixations.empty else _words 

6493 trials_per_participant = ( 

6494 trial_source.groupby("participant_id")["trial_id"].nunique() 

6495 if not trial_source.empty 

6496 else pd.Series(dtype=float) 

6497 ) 

6498 fixations_per_trial = ( 

6499 _fixations.groupby(["participant_id", "trial_id"]).size() 

6500 if not _fixations.empty 

6501 else pd.Series(dtype=float) 

6502 ) 

6503 words_per_trial = ( 

6504 _words.groupby(["participant_id", "trial_id"]).size() 

6505 if not _words.empty 

6506 else pd.Series(dtype=float) 

6507 ) 

6508 stats_df = pd.DataFrame( 

6509 [ 

6510 { 

6511 "Metric": "Trials per participant", 

6512 **safe_summary(trials_per_participant), 

6513 }, 

6514 {"Metric": "Fixations per trial", **safe_summary(fixations_per_trial)}, 

6515 {"Metric": "Words per trial", **safe_summary(words_per_trial)}, 

6516 ] 

6517 ).rename( 

6518 columns={ 

6519 "mean": "Mean", 

6520 "std": "Std", 

6521 "min": "Min", 

6522 "median": "Median", 

6523 "max": "Max", 

6524 } 

6525 ) 

6526 

6527 return { 

6528 "n_participants": len(participant_ids), 

6529 "n_texts": len(text_ids), 

6530 "n_trials": len(trial_ids), 

6531 "n_fixations": len(_fixations), 

6532 "n_words": len(_words), 

6533 "n_gaze": len(_raw_gaze), 

6534 "stats_df": stats_df, 

6535 } 

6536 

6537 

6538# Friendly field labels for the column-mapping summary, per source table. Box 

6539# fields are spelled out so the words table reads clearly (e.g. "Box left"). 

6540_WORD_MAPPING_LABELS = { 

6541 "participant": "Participant ID", 

6542 "trial": "Trial ID", 

6543 "word_id": "Word/IA ID", 

6544 "text": "Word text/label", 

6545 "text_id": "Text ID", 

6546 "line": "Line index", 

6547 "left": "Box left", 

6548 "right": "Box right", 

6549 "top": "Box top", 

6550 "bottom": "Box bottom", 

6551 "x": "Box x", 

6552 "y": "Box y", 

6553 "width": "Box width", 

6554 "height": "Box height", 

6555} 

6556_FIX_MAPPING_LABELS = { 

6557 "participant": "Participant ID", 

6558 "trial": "Trial ID", 

6559 "x": "X coordinate", 

6560 "y": "Y coordinate", 

6561 "duration": "Duration (ms)", 

6562 "timestamp": "Timestamp (ms)", 

6563 "fixation_id": "Fixation ID", 

6564 "text_id": "Text ID", 

6565 "word_id": "Word/IA ID", 

6566} 

6567_RAW_GAZE_MAPPING_LABELS = { 

6568 "participant": "Participant ID", 

6569 "trial": "Trial ID", 

6570 "x": "X coordinate", 

6571 "y": "Y coordinate", 

6572 "timestamp": "Timestamp (ms)", 

6573 "text": "Word text/label", 

6574} 

6575_MAPPING_TABLES = [ 

6576 ("Words/IA", "words", _WORD_MAPPING_LABELS), 

6577 ("Fixations", "fixations", _FIX_MAPPING_LABELS), 

6578 ("Raw gaze", "raw_gaze", _RAW_GAZE_MAPPING_LABELS), 

6579]

6581 

6582def _column_mapping_rows(mapping: dict) -> list[dict]: 

6583 """Flatten the stashed per-table schemas into one ``Table / Field / Mapped 

6584 column`` row list, dropping unmapped fields and joining composite trial ids.""" 

6585 rows: list[dict] = [] 

6586 for table_label, schema_key, labels in _MAPPING_TABLES: 

6587 schema = mapping.get(schema_key) 

6588 if not schema: 

6589 continue 

6590 for field_key, label in labels.items(): 

6591 col = schema.get(field_key) 

6592 if col is None: 

6593 continue 

6594 if isinstance(col, (list, tuple)): 

6595 col = " + ".join(str(c) for c in col) 

6596 rows.append( 

6597 {"Table": table_label, "Field": label, "Mapped column": str(col)} 

6598 ) 

6599 return rows 

6600 

6601 

6602# Field-key → canonical post-normalization column for each table. The remap 

6603# editor seeds from these (the normalized frame's columns ARE these names) so it 

6604# opens showing the current mapping. The word box always seeds x/y/width/height 

6605# because normalize_words converts edge coordinates to origin+size. 

6606_WORD_REMAP_CANON = { 

6607 "participant": "participant_id", 

6608 "trial": "trial_id", 

6609 "word_id": "word_id", 

6610 "text": "text", 

6611 "text_id": "text_id", 

6612 "line": "line_idx", 

6613 "x": "x", 

6614 "y": "y", 

6615 "width": "width", 

6616 "height": "height", 

6617} 

6618_FIX_REMAP_CANON = { 

6619 "participant": "participant_id", 

6620 "trial": "trial_id", 

6621 "x": "x", 

6622 "y": "y", 

6623 "duration": "duration_ms", 

6624 "timestamp": "timestamp_ms", 

6625 "fixation_id": "fixation_id", 

6626 "text_id": "text_id", 

6627 "word_id": "word_id", 

6628} 

6629_RAW_GAZE_REMAP_CANON = { 

6630 "participant": "participant_id", 

6631 "trial": "trial_id", 

6632 "x": "x", 

6633 "y": "y", 

6634 "timestamp": "timestamp_ms", 

6635 "text": "text", 

6636} 

6637# (table_key, label, field_specs, canonical-map) for the editable remap form. 

6638_REMAP_TABLES = [ 

6639 ("words", "Words/IA", WORD_FIELD_SPECS, _WORD_REMAP_CANON), 

6640 ("fixations", "Fixations", FIX_FIELD_SPECS, _FIX_REMAP_CANON), 

6641 ("raw_gaze", "Raw gaze", RAW_GAZE_FIELD_SPECS, _RAW_GAZE_REMAP_CANON), 

6642] 

6643# Validators keyed by table — checked before a remap is applied. 

6644_REMAP_VALIDATORS = { 

6645 "words": validate_word_schema, 

6646 "fixations": validate_fix_schema, 

6647 "raw_gaze": validate_raw_gaze_schema, 

6648} 

6649 

6650 

6651def _active_stored_dataset() -> Optional[tuple]: 

6652 """``(name, entry)`` for the active source when it's a stored upload, else 

6653 ``None`` — gates the editable remap form to stored datasets only.""" 

6654 name = st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") 

6655 entry = st.session_state.get("_datasets", {}).get(name) 

6656 return (name, entry) if entry is not None else None 

6657 

6658 

6659def _remap_proposed(schema: Optional[dict], frame_columns, canon: dict) -> dict: 

6660 """Seed the remap editor from the stored schema: each field the dataset had 

6661 mapped → its canonical column (present in the now-normalized frame), else 

6662 ``None``. The word box (canon ``_WORD_REMAP_CANON``) always seeds its four 

6663 geometry keys since normalize collapses any edge format to x/y/width/height.""" 

6664 cols = set(frame_columns) 

6665 schema = schema or {} 

6666 is_word_box = canon is _WORD_REMAP_CANON 

6667 proposed: dict = {} 

6668 for key, canonical in canon.items(): 

6669 if canonical not in cols: 

6670 proposed[key] = None 

6671 elif is_word_box and key in ("x", "y", "width", "height"): 

6672 proposed[key] = canonical 

6673 elif key == "text_id": 

6674 # text_id always exists post-normalization (falls back to trial_id); 

6675 # always seed it so a remap preserves text grouping instead of 

6676 # collapsing every reading of a text into its own trial_id. 

6677 proposed[key] = canonical 

6678 else: 

6679 proposed[key] = canonical if schema.get(key) else None 

6680 return proposed 

6681 

6682 

6683def _apply_remap() -> None: 

6684 """Re-derive the active stored dataset's frames under the edited mapping and 

6685 overwrite the entry in place (the "Apply remapping" button's ``on_click``). 

6686 

6687 Reads the per-table schemas captured during render in 

6688 ``_remap_pending_schemas``; validates each present table; on success 

6689 re-normalizes via ``data.remap_normalized_frame`` and recomputes the 

6690 composite trial components. ``app.main``'s stored-dataset branch then 

6691 re-publishes the new frames + mapping on the rerun this callback triggers.""" 

6692 active = _active_stored_dataset() 

6693 if active is None: 

6694 return 

6695 name, stored = active 

6696 pending = st.session_state.get("_remap_pending_schemas") or {} 

6697 problems: dict = {} 

6698 for table_key in ("words", "fixations", "raw_gaze"): 

6699 frame = stored.get(table_key) 

6700 if frame is None or frame.empty or table_key not in pending: 

6701 continue 

6702 probs = _REMAP_VALIDATORS[table_key](pending[table_key]) 

6703 if probs: 

6704 problems[table_key] = probs 

6705 if problems: 

6706 st.session_state["_remap_problems"] = problems 

6707 return 

6708 st.session_state.pop("_remap_problems", None) 

6709 

6710 new_entry = dict(stored) 

6711 new_schemas = dict(stored.get("schemas") or {}) 

6712 for table_key in ("words", "fixations", "raw_gaze"): 

6713 frame = stored.get(table_key) 

6714 if frame is None or frame.empty or table_key not in pending: 

6715 continue 

6716 schema = pending[table_key] 

6717 new_entry[table_key] = remap_normalized_frame(frame, schema, kind=table_key) 

6718 new_schemas[table_key] = schema 

6719 new_entry["schemas"] = new_schemas 

6720 # Recompute the composite trial components from the new trial mapping so the 

6721 # cascading trial picker stays in sync (mirrors the wizard finalize). 

6722 trial_schema = next( 

6723 ( 

6724 new_schemas[t].get("trial") 

6725 for t in ("fixations", "words", "raw_gaze") 

6726 if new_schemas.get(t) and new_schemas[t].get("trial") 

6727 ), 

6728 None, 

6729 ) 

6730 comp = trial_mapping_columns(trial_schema) if trial_schema else [] 

6731 new_entry["composite_trial_columns"] = comp if len(comp) > 1 else [] 

6732 st.session_state["_datasets"][name] = new_entry 

6733 st.session_state["_remap_applied"] = name 

6734 

6735 

6736def _render_remap_editor(name: str, stored: dict) -> None: 

6737 """Editable column-mapping form for a stored dataset (the surviving columns). 

6738 

6739 Renders one ``column_mapping_ui`` per present table seeded with the current 

6740 mapping, a note listing columns dropped at import, and an Apply button. The 

6741 widget keys are namespaced by dataset name so switching datasets never feeds 

6742 a stale column to a selectbox (which would raise).""" 

6743 st.subheader("Column mapping") 

6744 st.caption( 

6745 "Change how this dataset's columns map to the app's canonical fields. " 

6746 "Only columns that survived the original import are available." 

6747 ) 

6748 if st.session_state.pop("_remap_applied", None) == name: 

6749 st.success("Mapping updated — the dataset was re-derived.") 

6750 problems = st.session_state.get("_remap_problems") or {} 

6751 composite = list(stored.get("composite_trial_columns") or []) 

6752 pending: dict = {} 

6753 for table_key, label, specs, canon in _REMAP_TABLES: 

6754 frame = stored.get(table_key) 

6755 if frame is None or frame.empty: 

6756 continue 

6757 prefix = f"remap_{name}_{table_key}" 

6758 proposed = _remap_proposed( 

6759 (stored.get("schemas") or {}).get(table_key), frame.columns, canon 

6760 ) 

6761 # Composite trial id: pre-seed the multiselect with the preserved 

6762 # component columns (column_mapping_ui's ``proposed`` carries only a 

6763 # single default). Initial-seed only — never fight later user edits. 

6764 if composite and all(c in frame.columns for c in composite): 

6765 trial_key = f"{prefix}_trial" 

6766 if trial_key not in st.session_state: 

6767 st.session_state[trial_key] = list(composite) 

6768 pending[table_key] = column_mapping_ui( 

6769 frame, 

6770 label, 

6771 prefix, 

6772 specs, 

6773 proposed, 

6774 problems=problems.get(table_key), 

6775 use_expander=True, 

6776 # Here `proposed` is the dataset's current saved mapping (the frame is 

6777 # already normalized), not a fresh auto-detect — label it truthfully. 

6778 detected_label="currently mapped", 

6779 ) 

6780 st.session_state["_remap_pending_schemas"] = pending 

6781 

6782 dropped = stored.get("dropped_columns") or {} 

6783 flat = sorted({c for cols in dropped.values() for c in (cols or [])}) 

6784 if flat: 

6785 # A popover keeps the (often long) dropped-column list out of the way — 

6786 # zero footprint until opened, then a height-capped, searchable table. 

6787 with st.popover(f"⚠️ {len(flat)} columns dropped at import"): 

6788 st.caption( 

6789 "Dropped during the original import — re-upload the file to remap them." 

6790 ) 

6791 st.dataframe( 

6792 pd.DataFrame({"Dropped column": flat}), 

6793 hide_index=True, 

6794 width="stretch", 

6795 height=320, 

6796 ) 

6797 st.button( 

6798 "Apply remapping", 

6799 type="primary", 

6800 key=f"remap_apply_{name}", 

6801 on_click=_apply_remap, 

6802 help="Re-derive this dataset's frames with the new mapping (overwrites it).", 

6803 ) 

6804 

6805 

6806def _render_column_mapping_section() -> None: 

6807 """Show how each source column was mapped to the app's canonical fields. 

6808 

6809 For a stored uploaded dataset the mapping is **editable** — the user can 

6810 remap among the columns that survived normalization (``_render_remap_editor``). 

6811 Every other source is read-only, built from the schemas stashed by the 

6812 data-loading paths in ``app`` under ``st.session_state['_active_column_mapping']``.""" 

6813 active = _active_stored_dataset() 

6814 if active is not None: 

6815 _render_remap_editor(*active) 

6816 return 

6817 st.subheader("Column mapping") 

6818 mapping = st.session_state.get("_active_column_mapping") or {} 

6819 rows = _column_mapping_rows(mapping) 

6820 if not rows: 

6821 st.info("No column mapping available for the current data source.") 

6822 return 

6823 st.dataframe( 

6824 pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Table", "Field", "Mapped column"]), 

6825 hide_index=True, 

6826 width="stretch", 

6827 ) 

6828 st.caption("How each source column maps to the app's canonical fields.") 

6829

6831@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Building the derived analysis tables…") 

6832def _c_derived_tables( 

6833 _words: pd.DataFrame, 

6834 _fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

6835 _raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame, 

6836 words_fingerprint, 

6837 fixations_fingerprint, 

6838 raw_gaze_fingerprint, 

6839 pixels_per_degree_value: Optional[float], 

6840) -> dict: 

6841 """The six PRE-11/12/15/19 + AN-30 derived tables, built once per dataset. 

6842 

6843 PERF-3: **Data Inspection is a subtab**, and Streamlit renders every subtab's 

6844 body on every run — only the *display* is client-side. So this ran in full on 

6845 every rerun of the Scanpath view, whether or not the user had ever opened the 

6846 tab; a cosmetic colour change on the rail paid for the whole preprocessing 

6847 suite. Nothing here depends on any viz setting, so it is keyed on the three 

6848 frame fingerprints plus the one scalar that does matter (pixels-per-degree, 

6849 from the experimental setup). 

6850 """ 

6851 from scanpath_studio.measures import assign_fixations_to_words, enrich_fixations 

6852 from scanpath_studio.preprocessing import ( 

6853 character_grid, 

6854 cleaning_report, 

6855 saccade_table, 

6856 sentence_measures, 

6857 ) 

6858 

6859 measured_words = compute_word_metrics(_words, _fixations) 

6860 analysis_fixations = ( 

6861 enrich_fixations(assign_fixations_to_words(_fixations, _words), _words) 

6862 if not _fixations.empty and not _words.empty 

6863 else _fixations 

6864 ) 

6865 return { 

6866 "Sentences": sentence_measures(measured_words, _fixations), 

6867 "Saccades": saccade_table( 

6868 analysis_fixations, 

6869 pixels_per_degree=pixels_per_degree_value, 

6870 raw_gaze=_raw_gaze, 

6871 words=_words, 

6872 ), 

6873 "Trials": trial_summary_table(measured_words, _fixations), 

6874 "Readers": reader_summary_table(measured_words, _fixations), 

6875 "Characters": character_grid(_words), 

6876 "Cleaning QA": cleaning_report(_fixations), 

6877 }
